title: Kodak SlideTag digital photo frame doubles as Bluetooth tracker
content:
Kodak has announced a new collectible that builds on its Charmera line. After adding a Y2K‑inspired Millennium Edition to the Charmera collection earlier in the year, the company released a follow‑up to its tiny Kodak camera—a small digital photo frame that can display your shots.

The new device, called the Kodak SlideTag, also works as a Bluetooth tracker that is compatible with Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub tracking networks. It will retail for $34.99 each and, like the Charmera, will be sold in mystery boxes featuring a series of retro designs.
summary: The Kodak SlideTag is a tiny digital photo frame that also works as a Bluetooth tracker compatible with Apple’s Find My or Google’s Find Hub. It will sell for $34.99 each and will be offered in retro designs packaged in mystery boxes.
author: The Verge

title: Apple iPhone Duo review: folding iPhone priced at £1,999, the brand’s costliest smartphone
content:
The Apple iPhone Duo, Apple's first folding phone, has been described as early‑adopter gold that changes how iOS operates and condenses a tablet into a pocket‑sized device. The review notes that the Duo is not for everyone, as it upends the usual order of things with some interesting choices about how users interact with a phone – for better or worse.  

Priced at £1,999 (€2,299/$1,999/A$3,499), the Duo is Apple's most expensive smartphone. It costs more than most folding Android rivals and equals the combined price of the iPhone 18 Pro Max and the latest iPad mini.
summary: The Apple iPhone Duo is the company’s first folding phone, which changes how iOS works and condenses a tablet into a pocket. It is Apple’s most expensive smartphone at £1,999 (€2,299/$1,999/A$3,499), costing more than most folding Android rivals and as much as the iPhone 18 Pro Max and the latest iPad mini combined.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine behind drone strikes on two Russian ships off Libya
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was responsible for drone strikes on two Russian ships off Libya. The comment followed a separate incident on Saturday in which a drone hit a Russian cargo vessel in the eastern Baltic Sea near Finland, and Finnish border guards identified the strike as Ukrainian.
summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said Ukraine was responsible for drone strikes on two Russian ships off Libya. The attacks followed a drone hit on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday near Finland, which the Finnish border guard said was Ukrainian.
author: Euronews

title: Satellite images show Russian warship capsized in Benghazi after suspected drone attack
content: Satellite images reveal a Russian naval vessel capsized in the port of Benghazi, eastern Libya, after an explosion on Sunday. Local authorities say a drone attack is suspected, though they have not confirmed the responsible party.
summary: Satellite images show a Russian naval vessel capsized at the port of Benghazi in eastern Libya following an explosion on Sunday. Local authorities suspect a drone attack but have not confirmed who was responsible.

title: Sanctions, summits and strikes: The war in Ukraine shows no sign of slowing
content: Leo Cendrowicz’s Monday newsletter notes that the war in Ukraine continues unabated, with “more bombing of Ukraine” reported this week. The same issue also describes a “metaphorical bombing” of the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, underscoring ongoing tensions amid sanctions, summits and strikes linked to the conflict.
summary: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here, bringing you the Monday newsletter.

title: Turkish authorities search for lion spotted near Istanbul outskirts
content: Turkish authorities are conducting a search for a lion reported on the outskirts of Istanbul. The National Parks Directorate said specialist veterinarians and teams equipped with thermal‑imaging cameras are assisting the effort, concentrating the search on a wooded area.
summary: Turkish authorities are searching for a lion that was spotted on the outskirts of Istanbul. The National Parks Directorate said specialist veterinarians and teams equipped with thermal imaging cameras are assisting the search in a wooded area.

title: Thousands gather on Copacabana beach for Rio's 31st Pride Parade on Nov 22, 2026
content:
On Sunday 22 November 2026, thousands gathered on Copacabana’s beachfront in Rio de Janeiro for the city’s 31st Pride Parade.  

The celebration featured colourful costumes and dancing as participants honored LGBT+ diversity and called for greater equality.
summary: Thousands of people filled Copacabana's beachfront in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on Sunday 22 November 2026. The gathering was the city's 31st Pride Parade, celebrating LGBT+ diversity and calling for greater equality.

title: Rescuers recover 24 body bags from burnt-out confectionery factory near Jakarta
content: A fire gutted a confectionery factory near Jakarta, prompting authorities to recover 24 body bags from the wreckage. Rescue workers remain on site searching for missing employees while investigators examine the cause of the blaze.
summary: A fire gutted a confectionery factory near Jakarta, and authorities recovered 24 body bags from the wreckage. Rescue workers continue searching for missing employees as investigators examine the cause.
author: Euronews

title: Thousands rally in Istanbul against Turkey's crackdown on opposition and media
content: Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday to protest what they described as a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media. The demonstration was organized by the main opposition Yeni Parti after police raided Sozcu TV, arrested senior staff and a government‑appointed trustee was installed at the broadcaster, echoing similar actions against other independent outlets.
summary: Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday to protest a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media. The protest was organised by the opposition Yeni Parti after authorities installed a government‑appointed trustee at Sozcu TV following a police raid and arrests of senior staff.

title: Zelensky says Ukraine drone attacks sank Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi
content: President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Monday that Ukraine’s military carried out drone attacks on two Russian vessels in the Libyan port of Benghazi on Sunday. He said the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk in the strike. A liveblog provides ongoing updates.
summary: Ukraine’s military carried out drone attacks on two Russian vessels at the Libyan port of Benghazi on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that the Russian corvette Merkury had been sunk in the attack.
author: France 24

title: Marseille lose 3-2 at home to Le Mans after leading 2-0
content: Olympique de Marseille were beaten 3‑2 at home by Le Mans in Ligue 1. Marseille led 2‑0 after 40 minutes, with goals from Gouiri in the 33rd minute and Paixão in the 40th, before conceding three unanswered goals and losing the match.
summary: Olympique de Marseille were beaten 3-2 at home by Le Mans. Marseille had taken a 2-0 lead with goals from Gouiri in the 33rd minute and Paixão in the 40th minute before conceding three.
author: France 24

title: Pacific island nations voice despair over UN climate talks' failure at COP31
content: Several Pacific island nations expressed despair and disappointment Monday over the failure of the UN climate talks to reach a final agreement on tackling the climate crisis. Small nations in the Pacific are among the world's most vulnerable to the rising sea levels brought on my man-made global warming.
summary: Several Pacific island nations said they were disappointed on Monday after the UN climate talks failed to reach a final agreement at COP31. They noted they are among the world’s most vulnerable to sea‑level rise caused by man‑made global warming.
author: France 24

title: Experts: Israel's Gaza assault creates toxic wasteland with contaminated air, soil, water
content: Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’ Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report. Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.
summary: The Oxfam and Conflict and Environment Observatory report says Israel’s military assault has spread heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos and sewage across Gaza’s air, soil and water. Scientists and satellite data warn the contamination poses grave public‑health threats to Palestinians for generations.
author: Guardian World

title: Officials say Andy Burnham not backtracking on closer EU links
content:
Officials have told the Guardian that Andy Burnham is not backtracking or delaying his aim to forge closer links with the European Union, despite indications of a slower timetable after a recent summit in Brussels. Insiders say the government wants to let the pending trade deal “breathe a bit” and have dismissed speculation that No 10 is scaling back its ambitions.

The prime minister has pledged to outline options for the United Kingdom’s long‑term relationship with the EU, including the possibility of rejoining, with details to be set out later in the year.
summary: Andy Burnham is not backtracking or delaying his ambitions to create even closer links with the EU, officials said. The prime minister has promised to set out options for the UK's long‑term relationship with the EU, including the possibility of rejoining, later this year.
author: Guardian World

title: Andy Burnham briefs MPs on EU reset deal pending tuition fee dispute
content:
The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed European Union, noting the bloc’s shift toward a far‑right presence, a protectionist economic agenda and expanding defence ambitions. In this context, Andy Burnham’s recent “reset” with the EU has drawn attention from the original Brexit supporters, who see it as an opportunity to reconvene their campaign.

Parliament is set to revisit arguments about whether the United Kingdom should rejoin the EU after Burnham briefs MPs on a deal he agreed to on Friday. The briefing follows a deal described as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK‑EU relations. While the core agreements of the deal have not yet been ratified by EU member states, the EU has indicated it will not sign off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students.

Burnham is described as “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, though the briefing notes that any progress on that objective is not expected before the next general election. The discussion of the reset therefore adds a new dimension to ongoing parliamentary debate over the United Kingdom’s long‑term relationship with the European Union.
summary: Andy Burnham briefed MPs on a Friday deal that resets the UK’s relationship with the EU. The agreement has not been ratified by EU member states and will not be signed until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students.
author: Guardian World

title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian Merkury warship in Benghazi, Libya
content: President says Kyiv responsible for sinking Merkury warship in Benghazi on Sunday and also drone attack on cargo vessel MV Angara Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack Zelenskyy also said that “partners” – presumably the US – want the fourway talks between Ukraine, Russia, the US and Europe to take place before Christmas. “We are ready to do this literally tomorrow. We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner, and we must come to this meeting with a clear agenda, prepared and agreed by all of us.” “ When the main question comes up, ‘what happens after this war?’, our common answer must be security. Real security. Security for Ukraine, security for all of Russia’s neighbours, security for Europe and the entire Euro-Atlantic area. This is only possible if we work together as closely as possible. I believe this is only possible when Russia has no temptation to test whether security guarantees really work with Nato.”
summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv was responsible for sinking the Russian warship Merkury in Benghazi and for a drone attack on the cargo vessel MV Angara. He added that partners want four‑way talks among Ukraine, Russia, the United States and Europe to take place before Christmas.
author: Guardian World

title: Football Queensland $5 gate fee sparks club and family revolt
content: Football clubs that serve hundreds of thousands of players are set to break away from Football Queensland this week, saying the state governing body imposes fees they deem unreasonably high and lacks accountability. The dispute includes a $5 gate fee charged to parents and siblings who attend children’s matches in parts of regional Queensland. That fee is added to an annual cost that families already pay, which ranges from $300 to $700 per family. The clubs and families are organizing a revolt over these charges.
summary: Football Queensland $5 gate fee sparks club and family revolt.
author: Guardian World

title: Constitutional scholar Anne Twomey calls Australia defence bill ‘lazy and irresponsible’
content:
Australia’s new defence legislation has drawn sharp criticism from constitutional law expert Professor Anne Twomey, who described the bill as “lazy and irresponsible” lawmaking. Twomey said the lack of proper debate around the measure was “flabbergasting” and warned that provisions allowing the government to secretly classify any facility as a special security zone could raise serious legal issues. She added that the bill reflects an increasing trend of ministers exercising discretionary powers without parliamentary oversight.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese responded to criticism of the “accelerating capability and protecting bases” bill by saying opponents were “jump[ing] at shadows” and making “absurd” claims. Parliamentary crossbenchers opposed to the legislation, which was rushed through parliament with little public scrutiny, joined Twomey in voicing alarm over the expansion of ministerial powers.
summary: Constitutional scholar Anne Twomey calls Australia defence bill ‘lazy and irresponsible’.
author: Guardian World

title: Amazon launches first internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
content:
Amazon is set to launch a new batch of its internet satellites on Monday, November 23. An Ariane 6 rocket will carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites from the European Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana. The launch window opens at 6:09 a.m. Eastern Standard Time (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou) and is scheduled to last 29 minutes. Viewers can watch the event live on Space.com, with coverage beginning about 30 minutes before lift‑off.

The Amazon Leo constellation is designed to operate in low‑Earth orbit and will compete with SpaceX’s Starlink network, which currently has more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon plans a total of over 3,200 satellites for its network; to date, roughly 400 have reached orbit. The November 15 launch that was intended to deliver 40 additional satellites failed when a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur rocket suffered a problem shortly after liftoff, causing the loss of those spacecraft.

Amazon has booked additional rides on other launch vehicles, including ULA’s Atlas V, Blue Origin’s New Glenn, and SpaceX’s Falcon 9. The Vulcan Centaur will remain grounded while ULA investigates the failure. New Glenn has not flown since April, when it failed to place AST SpaceMobile’s BlueBird 7 satellite into the correct orbit, and it exploded during a pre‑launch test on May 28.

The Ariane 6, which debuted in July 2024, has completed nine launches, all successful except its maiden mission, which was a partial failure. The November 23 flight will be the fourth Amazon Leo mission launched by Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.
summary: An Ariane 6 rocket launched 36 Amazon Leo satellites from Kourou, French Guiana, eight days after a Vulcan Centaur failure destroyed 40 spacecraft. This mission marks the fourth Amazon Leo flight for Ariane 6 and the first since the November 15 launch anomaly.
author: Space.com

title: Max Verstappen wins Las Vegas F1 GP after final-lap Ferrari collision
content:
Max Verstappen secured a dramatic victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after a race characterized by intense competition and on-track incidents. The Dutch Red Bull driver led the final lap to claim the win, capping off a contest in which the lead changed hands 34 times. Despite being under siege throughout the event, Verstappen maintained his position to finish ahead of his rivals.

The race featured a collision between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, adding to the spectacle of the event. The article describes the competition as an old-school duel involving slipstreaming, noting that it provided a significant display for the sport. Verstappen’s performance is highlighted as evidence of his status among Formula One’s greats, with the unique nature of the race attributed to the specific conditions of this season.
summary: Max Verstappen secured victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix after Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton collided on the final lap. The race featured 34 lead changes, with the Red Bull driver maintaining the lead throughout the decisive final lap.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mets Seal $450M, 9-Year Deal with Pitcher Tarik Skubal
content: The New York Mets have reportedly signed free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal to a nine-year contract worth $450 million, marking the largest deal for a pitcher in Major League Baseball history. According to a report by Jon Heyman of The New York Post, this agreement surpasses the previous record held by Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who signed a 12-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers in 2024. The move represents the biggest transaction of MLB’s current offseason for the Mets, a team that has missed the playoffs for the last two seasons.
summary: The New York Mets signed free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal to a $450 million, nine‑year contract, the largest pitcher deal in MLB history. The previous record was a $325 million, 12‑year contract for Yoshinobu Yamamoto with the Dodgers in 2024.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pochettino’s New Manager Bounce Falls Flat After De Ligt Move
content:
Manchester United’s decision to pick a Dutch defender over Harry Maguire backfired when the team collapsed in the Anfield bearpit, losing 4‑0 to Liverpool, United’s fiercest rivals.  

The defeat marked the poorest opening result of the eight managers who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino, the loss has left the manager in despair.
summary: Manchester United fell apart in a 4-0 loss to Liverpool at Anfield after choosing the Dutch defender over Harry Maguire. The defeat, the worst opening result of the eight managers since Sir Alex Ferguson, left Mauricio Pochettino in despair.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bills defeat Dolphins, Bears maintain strong start, Ravens suffer sixth loss
content:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen was limited to a four-yard touchdown pass and two interceptions in a win over the Miami Dolphins, while the team’s defense secured the victory against the injury-depleted rivals. James Cook contributed a one-yard rushing touchdown and 89 yards on the ground, becoming the NFL’s second player to score a touchdown and top 75 rushing yards in nine consecutive games. The Bills improved to a 9-1 record, while Miami fell to 1-9 after losing four straight games, marking their worst start to a season since opening 2007 with a 0-13 record.

In other NFL results, the Kansas City Chiefs and Detroit Lions continued their strong starts, while the Baltimore Ravens suffered their sixth consecutive loss. The Chicago Bears also maintained their strong start to the season. Additionally, Michael Metcalf was ejected for an eye poke during a loss for the Pittsburgh Steelers, as noted in the roundup’s headline.
summary: Bills defeat Dolphins, Bears maintain strong start, Ravens suffer sixth loss.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alcaraz defeats Zverev 6‑2, 7‑6 to win first ATP Finals title
content:
Carlos Alcaraz captured his first ATP Finals title after defeating Alexander Zverev 6‑2, 7‑6 (7) in the final.  The Spaniard, who is the new world No 1, became the fourth player to win both a career Grand Slam and the ATP Finals.

The match underscored that the ATP world No 1 ranking and the title of the best male tennis player are held by different players.  This distinction had been apparent throughout the season, but it was highlighted again in the grand finale.

Alcaraz’s season had been hampered by a wrist injury that kept him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer.  Despite that setback, he completed the two most important objectives on his to‑do list for the year.
summary: Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev 6‑2, 7‑6 (7) to win his first ATP Finals title. The match confirmed Alcaraz as the new world No 1 while the titles of ATP world No 1 and best male player remain separate.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pochettino slams Yoro red card as Man United suffer 4-0 debut loss to Liverpool
content:
Manchester United lost 4‑0 to Liverpool at Anfield, marking the club’s joint‑heaviest debut defeat. Mauricio Pochettino said Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off early and that Manchester United were denied a penalty earlier in the match.

The 4‑0 result matched Lal Hilditch’s 1926 record of losing a first United game by that scoreline. Manchester United have conceded 34 goals across all competitions this season, the most by any team in Europe’s top five leagues.
summary: Manchester United were beaten 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield, matching the joint‑heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history. Manager Mauricio Pochettino said Leny Yoro’s red card was wrong and that United had been denied a penalty earlier in the match.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United eye move for Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney
content: Manchester United are reportedly eyeing Al‑Ahli striker Ivan Toney. Fulham are holding contract talks with Calvin Bassey, while Paris Saint‑Germain may step up their pursuit of Eli Junior Kroupi.
summary: Manchester United are looking to sign Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney. Fulham are holding contract talks with Calvin Bassey, and PSG may increase their pursuit of Eli Junior Kroupi.

title: Gerwyn Price Wins Grand Slam of Darts After Four-Year Wait
content: Gerwyn Price secured his first major PDC title in four years by defeating Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final. Price won the match with a score of 16-11, ending his long wait for a major championship victory.
summary: Gerwyn Price defeated Gian van Veen 16-11 in the Grand Slam of Darts final. The victory ended his four-year wait for a major PDC title.

content: Mauricio Pochettino said that even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool, given Manchester United’s circumstances. He questioned whether the Red Devils should have done more in their defeat.
summary: Mauricio Pochettino says even the best team could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances. He questions whether the Red Devils should have done more in their defeat.

title: Rio Ngumoha Impresses in Liverpool's 4-0 Win Over Manchester United
content: Match of the Day pundit Danny Murphy highlighted Rio Ngumoha’s performance in Liverpool’s 4-0 victory over Manchester United. Murphy explained that Ngumoha demonstrated his capabilities, describing him as a game-changer for the team.
summary: Danny Murphy, a Match of the Day pundit, praised Rio Ngumoha for his performance. Ngumoha helped Liverpool secure a 4-0 victory over Manchester United.
author: BBC Sport

title: Democratic National Committee Lays Off Key Staff After Recent Digital Operations Cuts
content: The Democratic National Committee has announced recent layoffs in its digital operations, affecting many staff who contributed to the party’s recent electoral success. Critics argue that the DNC must maintain permanent infrastructure to preserve the momentum it has built as it prepares for the 2028 election.
summary: The Democratic National Committee recently laid off many employees in its digital operations. Critics argue the committee must maintain permanent infrastructure to sustain momentum toward the 2028 election.

title: US Ports Hit by AI-Enabled Cyberattacks, Corpus Christi Faces Thousands Daily
content: A growing number of U.S. ports are reporting a surge of cyberattacks, many of which are AI‑enabled and target key infrastructure. The Port of Corpus Christi, Texas, the nation’s largest oil export passage, stated it was hit with “hundreds if not thousands” of attacks daily.
summary: US Ports Hit by AI-Enabled Cyberattacks, Corpus Christi Faces Thousands Daily.
author: The Hill

content: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) on Sunday said he would pass a single-payer healthcare bill — commonly referred to as “Medicare for All” — with the name “TrumpCare,” adding that he does not “really care what it’s called.” During El-Sayed’s interview with NBC News’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday, host Kristen Welker noted that President Trump…
summary: El-Sayed to rename Medicare for All as “TrumpCare”.
author: The Hill

title: Democrats secure largest House majority in decades after 2026 midterm wins
content: Democrats have secured the largest House majority in a regular election in decades, buoyed by significant 2026 midterm gains in historically challenging regions. Decision Desk HQ projects the party will hold 258 seats in the next Congress.
summary: Democrats have secured the largest House majority in a regular election in decades, following their 2026 midterm victories in historically challenging regions. Decision Desk HQ projects the party will hold 258 seats in the next Congress.
author: The Hill

title: Jeffries to Lead Largest Democratic Caucus Since 1990s, Faces Investigation Challenges
content:
Jeffries is set to lead the largest Democratic caucus since the 1990s, facing growing pains from policy disagreements and sprawling investigations.  

Democrats celebrated after exceeding midterm expectations, picking up almost 50 new House seats.
summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N. Y.) is set to take over the largest Democratic Caucus since the 1990s, and with it, potential headaches stemming from policy disagreements and sprawling investigations.
author: The Hill

title: Lawmakers pause for Thanksgiving as year‑end agenda approaches
content:
Lawmakers are home for Thanksgiving, but the holiday break will be brief as they prepare to return to a packed legislative agenda.  

With Democrats slated to take control of both chambers in January, Republicans have only a few weeks left to advance their priorities before the clock on their power expires.
summary: Lawmakers are home for Thanksgiving but will have little time to enjoy the break before returning to a packed legislative agenda. Democrats are set to take control of both chambers in January, leaving Republicans only a few weeks to push through their priorities before their power expires.
author: The Hill

title: Russian ship in Benghazi hit by suspected Ukrainian drone attack
content: Libyan officials reported that the Russian navy corvette Merkury, docked at a naval base in Benghazi, sustained severe damage during a suspected Ukrainian drone attack on Sunday. The vessel was struck by two sea drones, which triggered an explosion and a fire. An initial investigation into the incident is currently underway.
summary: The Russian navy corvette Merkury docked at a Benghazi naval base was struck by two sea drones, causing an explosion and fire. Libyan officials say the attack is suspected to be Ukrainian.
author: The Hill

title: Mayor Mamdani releases 84,000 additional 9/11 records
content:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) released an additional 84,000 records related to the September 11, 2001 attacks.  
The release follows a prior disclosure that revealed city leaders had lied about air quality. Mamdani said that after the terror attacks and the resulting health consequences, New Yorkers across the five boroughs demanded transparency.
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) released 84,000 additional records related to the September 11, 2001 attacks. The release followed a prior one that revealed city leaders had lied about air quality.
author: The Hill

title: Most governments reject meaningless agreement at Cop31 in Antalya
content:
The recent failure of COP31 in Antalya marked a “line in the sand” moment, according to Bill Hare. Nations stood together against major fossil‑fuel producers and rejected the draft text, a move Hare describes as a victory for multiculturalism. The agreement they turned down barely acknowledged the catastrophic climate emergency facing the world, nor did it signal a decisive shift away from fossil fuels.

Hare notes that the “good news” is that most governments rejected an agreement “stripped of meaning.” He also highlights the need for scrutiny of the influence wielded by Saudi Arabia, a key fossil‑fuel producer, in the negotiations.

Finally, Hare points out that co‑chairing global climate talks is not something that should be repeated, especially not by Australia. He concludes that the experiment “didn’t work.”
summary: Most governments at Cop31 in Antalya rejected an agreement stripped of meaning. Australia will not co‑chair future global climate talks, and Saudi Arabia's influence is under scrutiny.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Cannabidiol ineffective for behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability
content: A world‑first randomized controlled trial has determined that cannabidiol (commonly referred to as CBD) is not effective for treating severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability.
summary: A world-first randomized controlled trial found that cannabidiol is not effective in treating severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability. The study concluded that CBD does not help with these issues.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cellas Hayes investigates blood vessel damage's link to memory loss
content: A new study by Cellas Hayes, Ph. D., of the University of Kentucky investigates how damage to brain blood vessels may contribute to memory loss. The research suggests that vascular changes can play a role in cognitive decline, offering a perspective beyond the usual focus on Alzheimer’s disease.
summary: Alzheimer's disease is often the focus when someone develops memory problems. But changes in the brain's blood vessels may also be part of the picture—and new research by the University of Kentucky's Cellas Hayes, Ph.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Expert Mateusz Łabuz warns AI erodes trust and ability to discern reality
content: Mateusz Łabuz warns in his new book, The End of Reality, that generative AI poses a danger beyond technical glitches. According to Łabuz, it gradually erodes our ability to discern what is real, undermines trust in institutions, and hampers independent thinking.
summary: Mateusz Łabuz says generative AI is causing a slow erosion of people's ability to tell what is real, trust institutions, and think for themselves. He presents these warnings in his new book, The End of Reality.
author: Phys.org

title: Common drugs may cause lasting gut microbiome changes, study finds
content: A study of more than 2,500 people found that medications taken years or even long ago can produce lasting changes in the gut microbiome. Researchers identified microbial “fingerprints” from common drugs such as antidepressants, blood pressure medications, and anxiety treatments, persisting after cessation. Some anxiety medications produced effects comparable to broad‑spectrum antibiotics.
summary: A study of more than 2,500 people found that medications taken years ago can leave lasting changes in the gut microbiome. Researchers reported that common drugs including antidepressants, blood pressure medications and anxiety treatments leave microbial fingerprints, with some anxiety medications showing effects comparable to broad‑spectrum antibiotics.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Identify Gene That Helps Brain Immune Cells Contain Alzheimer Plaques
content: Scientists have identified a gene that enables brain immune cells to contain harmful plaques associated with Alzheimer’s. In mouse studies, malfunction of this gene accelerated toxic buildup and caused cognitive decline, suggesting that restoring its function could protect the brain.
summary: Scientists have identified a gene that helps brain immune cells contain harmful plaques linked to Alzheimer’s. In mice, when the gene malfunctioned, toxic buildup accelerated and cognitive abilities declined, suggesting that restoring its function could protect the brain.
author: Science Daily

title: Brown University discovers relativity alters heavy atom triple bonds
content:
Brown University researchers have reported a surprising discovery that challenges a long‑standing textbook explanation in chemistry. The study provides direct evidence that Einstein’s theory of relativity alters the way heavy atoms form triple bonds.

According to the researchers, relativistic effects cause normally distinct types of chemical bonds to blend together. This finding confirms a prediction that has been circulating for decades and suggests that the traditional rules of chemistry do not fully apply to heavy elements such as bismuth.
summary: Researchers at Brown University found direct evidence that Einstein's theory of relativity changes how heavy atoms form triple bonds, causing normally distinct types of chemical bonds to blend together. The discovery confirms a decades-old prediction and suggests that traditional chemistry rules do not fully apply to heavy elements such as bismuth.
author: Science Daily

title: AI tool finds bladder cancer warning signs up to five years early, detects 85% of cases
content:
Scientists have created an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85 % of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients.  

By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
summary: The AI tool can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a study of nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns missed by conventional screening, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.
author: Science Daily

title: Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher risk of Alzheimer’s, review of 40 studies finds
content: A major new review of 40 studies reports that individuals with type 2 diabetes have a 53 % higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. The analysis estimates that nearly five out of every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer’s each year. By concentrating on the relationship between these two conditions, the review aims to clarify a potentially serious link between metabolic health and brain health.
summary: A major new review of 40 studies found that people with type 2 diabetes have a 53% higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. Researchers estimate that nearly five out of every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer’s each year.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds gap suggests black holes form from stars that skip supernova
content: Massive stars may be collapsing directly into black holes without generating the supernova explosions that astronomers normally anticipate. Researchers identified a surprising pattern in 257 observed black‑hole mergers, and they propose that these silent stellar disappearances could account for a substantial portion of the black‑hole population in the universe.
summary: Massive stars may quietly collapse into black holes without producing supernova explosions. A pattern in 257 black‑hole mergers suggests these silent stellar disappearances could explain a large population of black holes throughout the universe.
author: Science Daily

title: DNA component may have shielded early life from intense UV radiation
content: Scientists discovered that a component of DNA acts like a sunscreen, converting ultraviolet damage into forms that are easier to repair, which may explain how early life survived intense UV radiation on early Earth. The finding could help solve a decades‑old evolutionary mystery about life’s endurance under those harsh conditions.
summary: Scientists found that a key component of DNA can turn potentially destructive ultraviolet damage into a form that is easier to repair. The discovery may help solve a decades‑old evolutionary mystery about how life endured the harsh conditions of early Earth.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find 287 DNA variants linked to longevity in 194-year-old tortoise Jonathan
content: Jonathan, a 194‑year‑old giant tortoise, is the world’s oldest living land animal. Scientists studying his DNA have identified 287 distinct genetic variants that are associated with DNA‑repair mechanisms, inflammation control, insulin regulation and cancer suppression, offering a potential explanation for his exceptional longevity.
summary: Jonathan, a 194‑year‑old giant tortoise, is the world’s oldest living land animal. Researchers identified 287 unique genetic variants in his DNA that are associated with DNA repair, inflammation control, insulin regulation and cancer suppression.
author: Science Daily

title: Most England ICBs cut GP funding for NHS weight‑loss drug Mounjaro
content:
Patients in England may miss out on NHS weight‑loss injections after most integrated care boards (ICBs) withdrew funding for GP services. An inquiry by the GP magazine Pulse found that the drug, Mounjaro (tirzepatide), is no longer covered by many local services.

The investigation revealed that 21 of 36 ICBs have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring the medication. Nine ICBs never offered a local enhanced service, and only four still retain one.

The findings highlight a growing gap in access to the potentially life‑changing treatment for eligible patients.
summary: An inquiry by GP magazine Pulse found that 21 of 36 integrated care boards in England have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring Mounjaro, also known as tirzepatide. Nine ICBs never had a local enhanced service and only four still retain one, leaving many eligible patients at risk of missing NHS weight‑loss injections.
author: Guardian Science

title: Recent FAA, Outlook, and JPMorgan Chase outages signal more tech failures ahead
content:
Recent disruptions have highlighted the fragility of critical infrastructure. A nationwide FAA ground stop halted air traffic, a multi‑day Microsoft Outlook outage brought entire companies to a standstill, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase stopped transactions across the institution. These incidents underscore the growing frequency of major tech failures.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN that the American public must be ready for significant investment in upgrading systems and cybersecurity. He warned that any step change in technology—whether in compute or applications—will inevitably produce “bumps in the road.”

Microsoft President Brad Smith issued a statement in response to the outages, though the content of that statement was not detailed in the report.
summary: Over the past week, the United States experienced a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi‑day Outlook outage that halted companies, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN that further investment in system upgrades and cybersecurity will be needed as more technology disruptions are expected.
author: The Verge

title: Democrats win biggest US House majority in over three decades
content: Democrats have secured their largest majority in the U.S. House of Representatives in more than three decades. The result is described as a crushing blow to President Donald Trump and is expected to usher in two years of divided government, political confrontation and ambitious legislative battles.
summary: Democrats have secured their largest US House of Representatives majority in more than three decades. The outcome is described as a crushing blow to President Donald Trump and sets the stage for two years of divided government and ambitious legislative battles.

title: Morocco's Ramakech sculpture park features upside-down house and giant installations
content: Ramakech, an 11‑hectare sculpture park near Marrakech, showcases an upside‑down house, oversized furniture and figures with vegetable heads. French artist Jean‑François Fourtou created the installations, describing them as larger‑than‑life works that evoke childhood memories. The park’s surreal pieces invite visitors to experience a world turned upside down.
summary: The Ramakech sculpture park near Marrakech spans 11 hectares and includes an upside-down house, giant furniture and vegetable-headed figures. French artist Jean-François Fourtou created the larger-than-life installations to evoke childhood memories.
author: Euronews

title: Drone strikes damage homes and UN building in Khartoum, army blames Ethiopia
content: Drone strikes early Sunday damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Khartoum, Sudan’s capital. The Sudanese army blamed neighboring Ethiopia for carrying out the attacks, noting that drone warfare has intensified as the country’s four‑year‑old conflict continues.
summary: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Khartoum early Sunday. The army accused neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks as drone warfare intensifies in the country's four‑year conflict.

content: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank on Sunday, calling the acts “Jewish terrorism.” Israeli police opened an investigation into the attacks, which occurred nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.
summary: Gadi Eisenkot condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as Jewish terrorism on Sunday. Israeli police opened an investigation into the attacks, which came nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.

title: Russian ship hit by suspected drone attack at Benghazi port, no casualties
content: Libyan authorities in the east reported that a Russian vessel docked at Benghazi port was struck on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, producing a blast but causing no casualties. No group has immediately claimed responsibility, and the incident occurs as Ukrainian forces have increased long‑range barrages against Russia beyond the front lines.
summary: Libyan authorities said a Russian vessel docked at Benghazi was struck on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, causing a blast but no casualties. No immediate claim of responsibility was made, and the incident came as Ukrainian forces have stepped up long‑range attacks against Russia.

content: Drone strikes early Sunday damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Khartoum, Sudan’s capital. The Sudanese army blamed neighboring Ethiopia for the attacks, noting that drone warfare has intensified as the country’s four‑year‑old conflict continues.

title: EU states reject 11th‑hour deal, causing collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey
content: EU member states objected Sunday to adopting an 11th-hour deal at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey because it omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, according to the bloc's presidency. This issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is occurring amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fueled by the war in Iran.
summary: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th‑hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, prompting a collapse of progress at the COP31 summit in Turkey. The issue remains a major point of contention amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fueled by the war in Iran.

title: Le Pen denies receiving confidential info from suspected civil servant
content: Marine Le Pen denied that she received confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party. She said she could not confirm whether other party members had benefited from the alleged leaks.
summary: French far‑right leader Marine Le Pen denied receiving confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party. She said she could not say whether others in the party had benefited.

title: Trump holds third meme‑coin gala in Virginia as Democrats claim conflict of interest
content:
Donald Trump is set to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on Sunday night at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia. The dinner will reward top holders of Trump’s meme coin, amid ongoing accusations from Democrats that the president is improperly profiting from his crypto ventures.

According to the event’s website, the dinner will feature meet‑and‑greets with Trump supporters, including boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thompson, and mentalist Lior Suchard. The event is positioned as a celebration of the president’s cryptocurrency interests while critics continue to question the ethical implications of his involvement.
summary: Trump holds third meme‑coin gala in Virginia as Democrats claim conflict of interest.
author: Guardian World

title: US Army seeks emergency order to detonate bomb chemicals in Iowa despite safety concerns
content:
The U.S. Army plans to invoke emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid a court order that had paused the detonation of several tons of bomb‑making chemicals, saying that continued delays will increase danger as the weather turns colder.  

In a filing late Saturday, government lawyers told the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals that swift action is needed to protect Army personnel and surrounding communities, adding that protection of human health and the environment demands action now, not delay.
summary: US Army seeks emergency order to detonate bomb chemicals in Iowa despite safety concerns.
author: Guardian World

title: UK taxpayers hold over £1tn in offshore tax havens, HMRC data shows
content:
UK taxpayers now hold more than £1 trillion in offshore tax‑haven accounts, a figure that has crossed the £1 trillion threshold for the first time, according to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) data. The data, obtained by the TaxWatch thinktank through freedom‑of‑information requests, shows a 10 % rise in the total value of balances held in financial centres such as Jersey and Panama between 2022 and 2024.

The increase has sparked concerns about the potential impact on the public purse, as higher offshore holdings could translate into lost tax revenue for the United Kingdom. The figures represent the latest available data on UK taxpayers’ offshore balances.
summary: UK taxpayers hold more than £1tn in offshore accounts, according to HMRC data obtained by TaxWatch. The offshore balances rose 10% between 2022 and 2024, raising concerns about potential losses to the public purse.

title: US intelligence chief Jay Clayton says he trusts Trump’s “friend” label for Putin
content:
U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Sunday that he trusts President Donald Trump “completely” after Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China. Clayton was pressed about the comment in media appearances that followed the trilateral summit with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Trump drew criticism at home and abroad, and on Saturday posted a photo of himself shaking hands with Putin captioned “My Friend.” Clayton noted the president’s warm description despite Putin being described as a chief U.S. adversary.
summary: US director of national intelligence Jay Clayton said he trusts President Donald Trump “completely” after Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China. content:
Australian climate change minister Chris Bowen faces significant criticism for his role in the COP31 negotiations, where disagreements over fossil fuels created an unbridgeable gap between petrostates and climate reality. Although the failure is not solely his, the issue of naming fossil fuels as the primary driver of global heating remained a central point of contention.

Following a major speech at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dismissed claims that he failed to address this core problem. He noted that the speech was brief and that numerous elements were omitted, defending his approach to the discussion.
summary: Australia's climate change minister Chris Bowen will face a torrent of criticism after delivering a major speech to the UN climate talks in Turkey. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dismissed criticisms that he had not named burning fossil fuels as the main cause of catastrophic global heating, saying the short speech could omit many points.

title: Molly Meldrum, Australian music broadcaster and Countdown host, dies at 83
content:
Molly Meldrum, the longtime host of the television music program Countdown and a prominent promoter of Australian music, has died at age 83. According to his longtime friend and manager Mark Klemens, Meldrum passed away peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a hospital in Melbourne, a detail reported by the Guardian.

The Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer was widely celebrated for helping expose Australian artists to international audiences and for bringing global music to Australia. Tributes have poured in from figures such as Human Nature and Jason Donovan, underscoring his lasting impact on the industry.
summary: Molly Meldrum, an Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer known for hosting Countdown, died at age 83. He died peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a Melbourne hospital, according to his friend and manager Mark Klemens.

title: Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light Review: Best Portable Star Projector
content:
The Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light has emerged as a recommended option for consumers seeking a high-quality version of the viral gooseneck star projector. The device is powered via USB and features a flexible stalk, a slide slot, and a focus wheel mounted on the nose. While the projector bears a resemblance to standard models found on social media platforms like TikTok, YouTube, and Facebook, the reviewer notes that its larger lens provides significantly richer and clearer images than typical run-of-the-mill versions.

The product includes 13 swappable slides packed in a compact box. Of these, 10 feature astronomy-related images, including a black hole, the Magellanic Cloud, the Milky Way, and the Pillars of Creation. The remaining slides depict an angel and stars, a jellyfish, Santa, a T. Rex, and a whale and stars, with some images presented in black and white. The reviewer highlights that while some slides are artistic illustrations, others, such as the Pillars of Creation, are actual astronomical images. The static nature of the projections is a key distinction, as the device does not produce animated displays, contrary to some AI-generated advertisements that claim it can cast moving images like space whales.

In terms of functionality, the projector includes a four-hour shut-off timer for the projection mode and a 12-hour timer for the night light function. The flexible neck allows for easy adjustment, though the reviewer noted that some USB ports may have a tighter grip on the device. The projector can be powered by various USB sources, including laptops, desktops, chargers, and power banks, making it portable for use in different locations. The reviewer successfully tested the device using a TV’s USB socket and a power bank, emphasizing its convenience for on-the-go use.

The device is designed to be user-friendly, with no remote control or sound options required. The light portion warms up but does not get hot, making it safe for children to handle. The reviewer suggests that the projector is suitable for entertainment, relaxation, and education, potentially sparking interest in STEM subjects. While the selection of slides is considered ample, the lack of extra slide packs is noted as a minor disappointment. The projector is positioned as a pocket-friendly option that offers good value for money and portability, distinguishing it from larger, more complex models that may offer laser-dot stars or other features.
summary: It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. I’ve yet to see a fictional elderly craftsman begging you to buy his hand-carved telescopes; however, it has absolutely muddied the waters around this viral gooseneck Galaxy Projector Night Light.

title: SpaceX launches classified NROL-136 spy satellites from California
content:
SpaceX carried out a classified launch of the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) NROL‑136 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base on the California coast on November 22, 2026. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Launch Complex‑4E at 7:23 a.m. Eastern Time (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local). The launch marked the sixth NRO flight of the year, all of which have been executed with SpaceX’s Falcon 9.

Two minutes after liftoff, the first‑stage booster separated from the upper stage, which continued to carry the classified payloads into low‑Earth orbit. The booster then reversed course and landed at Landing Zone 4 about seven and a half minutes after launch. This was the 14th flight for booster B1097, which had previously launched NASA’s Sentinel‑6B, NROL‑172, USSF‑259 for the U.S. Space Force, and eight Starlink missions.

NROL‑136 is the 15th mission dedicated to building the NRO’s “proliferated architecture,” a network of satellites developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The constellation, begun in May 2024 with NROL‑146, is intended to increase coverage and improve the capability and resilience of U.S. intelligence operations in space. The agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL‑136 or details about their onboard technologies.
summary: SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California.

title: Marc Márquez Secures Record-Equalling Eighth MotoGP Title in Portugal
content:
Marc Márquez secured the 2026 MotoGP world title at the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday. Finishing eighth, he earned enough points to create an unassailable lead in the overall standings. The Ducati rider had to finish in the top nine to guarantee the championship, and after starting second on the grid, he rode cautiously to finish eighth, clinching the title with a round to spare.

Márquez’s eighth premier‑class title ties him with Giacomo Agostini for the most championships in motorcycle racing history, placing the Spaniard alongside the great at the top of the all‑time standings.
summary: Marc Márquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP world title at the Portuguese Grand Prix after an eighth-place finish gave him an unassailable lead. The Spaniard’s eighth premier‑class title ties him with Giacomo Agostini for the most in motorcycle racing history.

title: Manchester City’s WSL title bid hit by Spurs after Vinberg and Naz’s late double
content:
Tottenham Hotspur’s late double from Vinberg and Naz gave the home side a surprise victory over Manchester City, handing the Citizens their second consecutive defeat. The result pushed Spurs within three points of the European qualification places and denied City the chance to climb back to the top of the Women’s Super League table.

The loss came just 24 hours after Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool, a timing that intensified the impact on City’s title campaign. It was the first time Manchester City failed to win a home league match—and indeed the first home loss—during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16‑month tenure as manager.

title: Steve Borthwick Uses Eddie Jones Footage to Inspire England’s Record Win Over All Blacks
content: The head coach said he has watched videos from Eddie Jones’ time in charge to help England start matches strongly Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation: “We are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off.” And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep. Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand.
summary: Steve Borthwick watched videos from Eddie Jones’ tenure to help England start matches strongly. England’s emotional preparation, including a powerful response to the haka and a speech by Lewis Moody, helped the team achieve a record victory over the All Blacks.

title: Kildunne returns to haunt Harlequins as Bristol get PWR season off to a flyer
content:
Harlequins fell to Bristol 21‑48 in the Premiership Women’s Rugby opener, a match that saw former Harlequins full‑back Ellie Kildunne make a striking debut for her new club. Kildunne scored two tries against her former side, marking a strong return to the Stoop five months after her shock exit from Harlequins.

Kildunne’s performances had come under scrutiny in recent months, and she was dropped to the bench for England’s final two WXV matches in October. She responded in Bristol’s opening game with a “stellar and trademark” performance that silenced critics and demonstrated her continued quality.

Bristol head coach Scott Lawson had publicly backed Kildunne before the season, saying that playing at the West Country club would “bring the best” out of the 27‑year‑old. Her game‑changing presence drew defenders toward her, freeing the wings. Both back‑three wings, Reneeqa Bonner and Millie David, also scored two tries each in the victory.
summary: Bristol defeated Harlequins 48-21 in the Premiership Women’s Rugby opener, with full‑back Ellie Kildunne scoring two tries on her debut after returning to the Stoop. Wings Reneeqa Bonner and Millie David also scored two tries each, while coach Scott Lawson praised Kildunne’s impact.

Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected

title: Florida prisoners testify that concrete prison heat reached 119°F heat index
content: Temperatures in a concrete facility contributed to one man’s death after he struggled to breathe, prisoners allege On Tuesday afternoon Dwayne Wilson, 69, a thin Black man dressed in a light gray prison uniform, testified about the stifling heat he experienced in the Dade correctional institute, a concrete state prison south of Miami, Florida, without air conditioning. He removed his glasses and wiped his eyes as he spoke. “It was so hot,” he said, his voice catching. “It’s so hot sometimes you have to put water on the floor just to try to keep cool.” Wilson said he’s housed in the H dorms, a T-shaped building with one-to-two-person cells, nicknamed “hell dorm” by prisoners because its concrete walls radiate heat absorbed from the sun. The plaintiff’s law firm, the Florida Justice Institute, convinced a judge to allow 31 sensors to be temporarily installed throughout the prison during the summer of 2025. They recorded temperature and humidity levels that Stefano Shiavon, a professor of civil and environmental engineering with expertise in thermal comfort, used to calculate the heat index. He found it to be above 88F (31C) 97% of the time, with the highest heat indexes often recorded at night, including one reading in the H dorm dayroom equivalent to 119F (48C) at 10pm one July day last year. “The walls sweat,” Wilson said. “It’s miserable in the cell at night because, again, it’s so hot. No air comes to the bed we sleep at and the bed is soaked in sweat.”
summary: Florida prisoners testify that concrete prison heat reached 119°F heat index.

title: New transport pathway shows caveolin‑1 aids fat storage in cells
content:
Lipodystrophy is a serious metabolic disease defined by abnormal lipid storage, where ingested fats bypass adipose tissue and deposit in the liver, muscle, or heart. This redistribution leads to significant metabolic consequences, including fatty liver and type 2 diabetes, while the visible fat changes and associated symptoms cause considerable distress for patients.

The underlying causes of the condition may stem from a congenital gene mutation, an immune disorder, or an infection.
summary: Scientists have identified a new transport pathway that explains how caveolin‑1 helps cells store fat. In lipodystrophy, ingested fats are not stored in adipose tissue but accumulate in the liver, muscle, or heart, leading to fatty liver and type 2 diabetes.

content: Researchers at Hokkaido University have observed that silver can briefly adopt a rare crystal structure previously seen only in the radioactive element polonium. The discovery highlights how the atomic configuration of a material can dramatically influence its properties and may provide a pathway for investigating other materials with potentially useful characteristics.

content:

title: Binding of Isaac developer pulls AI music from Repentance Plus after Steam backlash
content:
The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has faced review-bombing on Steam after it was revealed that a Grand Theft Auto-themed segment utilized AI-generated music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff identified the tracks by finding audio files containing Suno metadata that linked to the generative AI platform. In response, creator Edmund McMillen posted on X, apologizing and stating he was unaware that the in-game parody featured generative AI music.

The controversy is compounded by the fact that Valve requires developers to disclose the use of generative AI in their development processes. Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind the title, is also implicated in the situation, though the provided text cuts off before detailing their specific response or actions.
summary: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus was review‑bombed on Steam after a Grand Theft Auto‑themed segment was found to contain generative AI music with Suno metadata. Creator Edmund McMillen apologized on X, saying he had no idea the GTA parody used AI music, and the developer removed the AI tracks.
author: The Verge

title: Delta flights delayed at Atlanta hub due to weight‑balance system outage
content:
All Delta Air Lines flights arriving at or departing from Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport are experiencing significant delays on Sunday. The airline attributes the slowdown to a malfunction in the system that calculates each aircraft’s weight and balance, a critical factor for safe operations.

Atlanta’s airport serves as Delta’s largest hub and ranks among the world’s busiest facilities. Although the current disruption is limited to Delta, airport officials note that prolonged delays could spill over to other carriers and airports that share the same infrastructure.

The incident follows a Federal Aviation Administration outage the previous week, which prompted a nationwide ground stop and resulted in thousands of flight cancellations. The New York Times reported that the weight‑and‑balance system went offline, prompting the present delays.
summary: All Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are experiencing significant delays on Sunday because of a problem with the system that calculates a plane's weight and balance. The issue currently affects only Delta, but could affect other airlines and airports if delays continue.
author: The Verge

title: Author tests smartwatches, rings, bands and earbuds to find best sleep trackers
content:
I tested a range of sleep‑tracking devices to determine which offered the most useful data for improving nightly rest. The review focused on smartwatches, smart rings, smart bands, sleep earbuds, and sleep masks, all of which record metrics such as time to fall asleep, duration of deep sleep, restlessness, resting heart rate, and potential breathing difficulties during the night.

The article explains that these devices can reveal how lifestyle choices affect sleep. For example, a late‑afternoon cappuccino might cause a restless night, while an evening workout could promote deeper sleep. By collecting and reviewing this information, users can identify patterns and make adjustments to their routines.

The piece concludes that the more detailed the sleep data, the greater the opportunity to improve sleep quality. It emphasizes that understanding these metrics is the first step toward achieving better rest.
summary: The author covered themselves in various sleep‑tracking devices—including smartwatches, smart rings, smart bands, sleep earbuds and sleep masks—to evaluate their monitoring capabilities. The devices reported metrics such as time to fall asleep, deep‑sleep duration, restlessness, resting heart rate and nighttime breathing issues, helping users link lifestyle habits to sleep quality.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
content: John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang ’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”. The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.
summary: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Four West Bank villages hit by suspected settler attacks, cars burned
content: Burnt‑out cars, damaged trucks and anti‑Arab graffiti were found in four Palestinian villages in the Israeli‑occupied West Bank on Sunday, 22 November 2026. Local activists blamed the overnight attacks on Israeli settlers.
summary: Burnt-out cars, damaged trucks and anti-Arab graffiti were discovered in four Palestinian villages in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday 22 November 2026. Local activists blamed the overnight attacks on Israeli settlers.
author: Euronews

title: Suspected drone strike hits Russian vessel in Benghazi port, prompting security concerns
content: A suspected drone strike damaged a Russian ship docked in Libya’s Benghazi port, prompting authorities to investigate the blast. The incident has heightened concerns about the spread of the Russia‑Ukraine conflict and raised fears for broader regional security.
summary: A suspected drone strike hit a Russian ship in Libya’s Benghazi port. Authorities are investigating the blast amid concerns about regional security and the spread of the Russia‑Ukraine conflict.
author: Euronews

title: Iranian tanker incident reported near US navy blockade line in Strait of Hormuz
content: Amid conflicting reports that an Iranian tanker left Kharg Island on Sunday to challenge the U.S. military blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, an incident was reported near the U.S. Navy blockade line. Iran warned that any U.S. attempt to stop its tankers would trigger immediate attacks.
summary: An incident involving an Iranian tanker was reported near the US navy blockade line in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran warned that any US attempt to stop its tankers would lead to immediate attacks.
author: Euronews

title: Barnham village holds symbolic vote to leave UK over plan to house 931 asylum seekers
content:
Residents of the English village of Barnham held a symbolic referendum on Saturday to vote for leaving the UK. This protest was directed against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base, a number exceeding the village’s population of 584. The action follows a similar protest in another village in September, illustrating rising tensions over immigration in the country.

Meanwhile, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed earlier this week. Despite this, supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive.
summary: Barnham village holds symbolic vote to leave UK over plan to house 931 asylum seekers.
author: France 24

title: Russian strike on Dymer apartment building north of Kyiv kills two
content: A Russian attack on Sunday hit an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, destroying a five‑storey structure. The strike killed at least two people and wounded four. Rescuers evacuated nine individuals, including a child, while at least 11 others are believed to remain trapped beneath the rubble.
summary: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The strike destroyed the five‑storey building, rescuers evacuated nine people including a child, and at least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.
author: France 24

title: Israeli probe after arson in three West Bank villages; Eisenkot calls it Jewish terrorism
content: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.
summary: Israeli probe after arson in three West Bank villages; Eisenkot calls it Jewish terrorism.

title: PSG beat Nice 3-2 to extend Ligue 1 winning run, lose Désiré Doué to knee injury
content:
PSG secured a 3‑2 win over Nice on Saturday, extending their winning run and tightening their hold on the top spot in Ligue 1.  
However, the match ended in disappointment as forward Désiré Doué suffered a serious knee injury, ruling him out for several months.
summary: PSG defeated Nice 3-2 on Saturday, extending their Ligue 1 winning streak and maintaining their lead at the top of the table. Forward Désiré Doué suffered a serious knee injury that will keep him out for several months.
author: France 24

title: Marine Le Pen denies receiving confidential leak from interior ministry official
content: Marine Le Pen, the French far‑right leader, said on Sunday that she neither received nor requested confidential information about an investigation into her party from a senior interior‑ministry official. She added that she could not confirm whether other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, denied the allegations and requested to be relieved of his duties while a probe proceeds.
summary: Marine Le Pen said on Sunday she did not receive or ask for confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. The senior civil servant, Hugues Moutouh, denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.

title: UK PM Andy Burnham reopens EU talks, sparking criticism from May and Johnson
content: “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” The words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear. But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind? Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson. So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead? France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.
summary: David Dimbleby announced the Brexit referendum result on 24 June 2016, saying “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels on a closer relationship with the EU, a move criticised by Theresa May and Boris Johnson.
author: France 24

title: Russian navy corvette hit by suspected Ukrainian sea drone at Benghazi base
content: A Russian navy corvette that was docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya was struck on Sunday by a sea drone that local officials say was suspected to be Ukrainian. The incident was described as part of the ongoing attacks linked to the Russia‑Ukraine war in the North African country. Hours after the corvette was hit, a cargo ship was also struck by a sea drone in a second attack off the coast of Benghazi later that evening.
summary: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a suspected Ukrainian sea drone, local officials said. Hours later a cargo ship was also struck by a sea drone in a second attack off Benghazi on Sunday evening.
author: France 24

title: Democrat Chuck Hubbard wins NC seat, clinching historic House majority
content: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the U.S. House from North Carolina on Sunday after winning a recount that unseated veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, the chair of the House Rules Committee. Hubbard’s victory secured at least 258 seats for Democrats in the 2026 midterm elections, the party’s strongest general‑election showing in decades.
summary: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.
author: France 24

title: Mexican military captures alleged Beltran Leyva gang leader “Chapo Isidro” in Sinaloa
content: Mexican special forces captured the alleged leader of the Beltrán Leyva cartel, identified as “Chapo Isidro,” after a raid and ensuing shootout in the coastal state of Sinaloa. Authorities said he was one of the FBI’s most‑wanted fugitives.
summary: The alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, known as “Chapo Isidro,” was captured by the Mexican military. The capture followed a raid and shootout in the coastal state of Sinaloa.

title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief says science leaves no doubt
content: COP31 ended on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to overcome divisions over fossil fuels, bringing two weeks of talks and two days of overtime to a close that UN Secretary-General António Guterres described as a “deeply disappointing” setback.
summary: COP31 concluded on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to bridge divisions over fossil fuels. UN Secretary‑General António Guterres called the result a “deeply disappointing” setback and warned there is no ambiguity in the science.

title: Afghan midwife Zahra returns to Herat unemployed after five years in Iran
content: Afghan women who have been forced to return from Iran are facing difficulties rebuilding their lives, as illustrated by 28‑year‑old Zahra. After five years caring for an elderly woman in Iran and earning enough to get by, she is now back in Herat, western Afghanistan, where she is unemployed and lives with her parents and siblings, while her six‑year‑old son stays with her ex‑husband.
summary: Zahra spent five years caring for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by. Back in Herat, western Afghanistan, the 28-year-old trained midwife is unemployed and lives with her parents and siblings while her six-year-old son lives with her ex-husband.

title: Theresa May’s Brexit remarks send Conservatives back to their unhappy place
content:
Theresa May appeared on BBC One at 9:45 am Sunday, promoting Brexit in a way that could be mistaken for a 2018 broadcast.  

The appearance underscores a challenge for the Conservative Party, as Andy Burnham’s push for closer EU ties forces the Tories back into a difficult position.

Andy Burnham’s decision to push back against closer EU ties is described as plunging the Conservative Party into its own unhappy place.

title: PIP review to recommend overhaul, keeping benefit for all ages
content:
A committee co‑led by Social Security Minister Stephen Timms is set to publish its final review of the Personal Independence Payment (PIP) this week, with the report expected as early as Tuesday. The recommendations will call for an overhaul of the benefit while retaining the system for all ages, contrasting with a separate Milburn review released last week that suggested partially scrapping the scheme for under‑25s.

The forthcoming findings will place Prime Minister Andy Burnham in a position to make a politically sensitive decision on the future of PIP.
summary: A committee co‑led by social security minister Stephen Timms will recommend overhauling the Personal Independence Payment system and retaining it for all ages. The final report is expected to be published as soon as Tuesday, presenting Prime Minister Andy Burnham with a politically sensitive decision.
