title: COP31 Draft Keeps Electrification Goal, Delays Adaptation Finance and Science Targets
content: After an evening of tense discussions, a new version of the cover text was finally released at around 2am on Sunday morning. The latest draft, which is scheduled to be put to a plenary session for approval at 9am – although delays look likely – retains a goal to boost electrification and links it more strongly with clean energy and storage. It does not, however, include language on transitioning away from fossil fuels as many countries had called for. It ditches a specific numerical target for carbon capture, use and storage (CCUS), a controversial technology that is favoured by fossil fuel producers, which is now only an aim “to achieve gigatonne scale globally by 2035 as a collective global aspiration”. The previous version had two alternative targets, a weaker one of 0.5Gt “working towards” 1.3-2.5Gt and a stronger one of 2.5Gt. The draft cover decision has strong language on responding to an almost certain overshoot of the 1.5C warming limit, recognising that it will increase loss and damage and result “in increasingly adverse, and in some cases irreversible, impacts and risks to human and natural systems”. As President of Negotiations Chris Bowen has repeatedly drawn attention to, this is the first COP held since the UN acknowledged that overshoot is inevitable. In pursuing efforts to limit any overshoot, the decision recognises the need for “deep, rapid and sustained reductions in greenhouse gas emissions in line with 1.5 °C pathways” – which is a push towards greater ambition. The text also resolves to close adaptation gaps and boost action and support to help countries and communities to better cope with adverse climate impacts. But it does not put a figure to a goal agreed at COP30 last year to triple adaptation finance by 2035. The goal did not specify a baseline year and African nations, least-developed countries and small island states had pushed for it to be a later and higher baseline and therefore a larger target number of $120 bn a year. Instead, the text launches a “roadmap” on adaptation finance to be considered at COP32. Loss and damage finance has been cut from the roadmap’s scope, as have references to about half the money pledged to the loss and damage fund having yet to be sent to the fund’s bank account and the gap between the $2.8 billion of loss and damage funding requested by developing countries in the fund’s start-up stage and the $0.342 billion allocated to fund these projects. “Erasing the shortfall doesn’t make it disappear for families who have lost everything”, said Harjeet Singh, global convenor of Fill the Fund. The new text drops its invitation to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) to publish all of its next three reports in time for the 2028 global stocktake of climate progress. Instead, it just invites them to “continue to provide policy-relevant information as input to the UNFCCC processes, including outputs from the seventh assessment cycle to the next global stocktake”. It no longer specifies that all their reports, including the third on reducing emissions, are published. The IPCC will have an online meeting in December to discuss this issue but COP31 guidance will be influential in its decision. As Climate Home News entered the venue around 7.30am, tired-looking negotiators from Saudi Arabia and from the Alliance of Small Island Developing States were seen entering the area which houses the Presidency’s offices, as others dozed on sofas. A source close to the German delegation said that negotiations had been intense and were not necessarily resolved. The post COP31 Bulletin Day 13: New draft retains electrification goal but delays adaptation finance and science decisions appeared first on Climate Home News.
summary: COP31 Draft Keeps Electrification Goal, Delays Adaptation Finance and Science Targets.
author: Climate Home News

title: Cop31 negotiators receive third draft deal as final plenary approaches
content:
On day 14 of the COP31 climate summit, a third version of the draft text was released overnight, according to organisers. Negotiators have now been convened for what the organisers describe as the final plenary session.

The discussions have been taking place at the Antalya Expo Centre in Turkey, where the co‑presidents of the conference—representing Australia and Turkey—have been meeting with a large number of countries late into the night. Despite these meetings, the talks have ground to a near halt on Saturday, with no resolution achieved.
summary: A third version of the draft text was published overnight and negotiators were called in for what organisers described as the final plenary session of Cop31. Talks stalled on Saturday as the co‑presidents of the conference from Australia and Turkey met with scores of countries late into the evening with little sign of resolution.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Single feathers could indicate if eastern black rails remain in Texas or migrate north
content:
A recent field observation describes a nighttime walk through a wetland. The observer drags a rope across the marsh, attaching several plastic bottles, each filled with two or three noisy cat toys. In the darkness the only sounds are the jingling of the toys, mosquitoes buzzing, and wetland grasses moving in the wind.

The accompanying headline refers to a separate study that suggests single feathers could indicate whether eastern black rails remain in Texas or migrate north. No details from the field walk support that claim, and the two pieces of information are presented independently.
summary: Researchers are conducting night surveys in Texas wetlands, dragging a rope with noisy cat toys to attract eastern black rails. They hope that analyzing a single feather will determine if the birds are resident in Texas or migrate north.
author: Phys.org

title: APOD November 22, 2026: Juno captures swirls and colors on Jupiter
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for November 22, 2026 showcases a color‑enhanced image of Jupiter captured by the Juno spacecraft. The image highlights the planet’s swirling cloud patterns and the bright, reddish regions that dominate the lower right of the frame.  

The accompanying explanation notes that the colors seen in Jupiter’s clouds are not produced by the planet’s main atmospheric constituents—hydrogen and helium, which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops. Instead, trace molecules are responsible, with small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide cited as a leading candidate. The image also illustrates a general trend: lighter clouds tend to lie higher in the atmosphere than darker ones. In this particular view, the lighter clouds encircle the reddish areas and appear to overlay some darker domains on the upper right.

The photograph was taken in 2018 during Juno’s 14th low‑pass over Jupiter. The spacecraft remains in a looping elliptical orbit, passing close to the planet every 33 days and surveying a slightly different sector with each orbit.  

The image credit goes to NASA, Juno, SwRI, and MSSS, with processing and license handled by Matt Breachy and Seán Doran. The APOD page lists Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, and Keighley Rockcliffe as authors and editors, and notes that the service is provided by ASD at NASA/GSFC, NASA Science Activation, and Michigan Tech. U.
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 22, 2026 features a color‑enhanced image of Jupiter’s clouds taken by NASA’s Juno spacecraft. The photo was captured in 2018 during Juno’s 14th low‑altitude pass and shows lighter clouds swirling above darker regions while the exact cause of the colors remains uncertain.
author: NASA News

title: UN diplomats leave Geneva talks on autonomous weapons without agreement
content:
UN diplomats in Geneva focused on developing rules for autonomous weapons, often called “killer robots.” After a week of largely fruitless negotiations, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” rather than reaching a binding agreement.

Prior to the talks, the International Committee of the Red Cross—guardian of the Geneva Conventions—called for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. This urgency was echoed by the UN Secretary‑General and Pope Leo. A compromise was reached, though the specific details were not disclosed.
summary: UN diplomats leave Geneva talks on autonomous weapons without agreement.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon adds shipping labels warning NYC Council could add $5 to orders
content:
Amazon is intensifying its opposition to the New York City Council’s proposed Delivery Protection Act. The company has begun attaching labels to shipments that state the council could add as much as $5 to any Amazon order. In addition, Amazon has started displaying notifications in its mobile app and on its website, warning customers about the potential charge.

The Delivery Protection Act would prohibit the third‑party arrangements Amazon currently relies on for many deliveries, including the use of small companies and independent contractors. Under the bill, last‑mile delivery firms that operate warehouses would be required to obtain city licenses and directly employ their workers. Amazon’s recent labeling and app alerts represent a new tactic in its broader campaign against the legislation.
summary: Amazon is placing labels on shipments that say the New York City Council could add up to $5 to any Amazon order. The labels are part of Amazon’s broader opposition to the Delivery Protection Act, which would bar third‑party delivery arrangements and require last‑mile firms to be city‑licensed and directly employ workers.
author: The Verge

title: American Airlines flight halted in Phoenix during longest nationwide aviation shutdown since 9/11
content:
After a series of disruptions at airlines, banks and major technology companies such as Microsoft and Apple, many people have begun to believe that the world’s systems are under attack. The growing sense of vulnerability is reflected in headlines that link seemingly unrelated incidents.

Nicole Reindorf, a 70‑year‑old passenger, was on an American Airlines flight that was ready to depart from Phoenix when the pilot announced the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since 9/11. Reindorf had just read headlines about a global Microsoft outage hours earlier and immediately suspected a connection between the two events, attributing them to AI‑related threats. She feared that the shutdown would prevent her from attending the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.
summary: After recent chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, a pilot announced the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since 9/11 on a flight ready for takeoff in Phoenix. Passenger Nicole Reindorf, 70, linked the shutdown to a global Microsoft outage and feared AI-related threats would cause her to miss a wedding in California.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Music amplifies youth-led protests in France as musicians voice demands
content: Protest songs have historically united people against war, racism, inequality and the establishment, and music is now a key element of the youth‑led demonstrations in France. Reporters visited the protests and spoke with musicians who are using their voices to convey the demonstrators’ demands.
summary: Music is playing a key role in the youth‑led demonstrations in France. Reporters met musicians who are using their voices to express the protesters’ demands.
author: France 24

title: 200+ ex-TPLF fighters surrender to Ethiopian army as Ethiopia-Eritrea border tension rises
content: State‑affiliated media reported that more than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military on Friday. The surrender occurs as troops mobilise along the Ethiopia‑Eritrea border amid escalating tensions, according to France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti.
summary: More than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military on Friday, according to state‑affiliated media. The surrender occurs as border tensions with Eritrea increase, reported by France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti.
author: France 24

title: Ethiopia entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed makes affordable reusable pads to fight period poverty
content: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is addressing period poverty and menstrual stigma by producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and conducting awareness campaigns in schools. She aims to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls remain in class, according to a report by Awa Diouf and Guillaume Gougeon.
summary: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is tackling period poverty and stigma by producing affordable reusable sanitary pads. She also raises awareness in schools to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class.
author: France 24

title: Thousands protest rising costs, education and military spending in France
content: France is preparing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with thousands expected to rally over rising living costs, education and military spending across France and Europe. Demonstrators are focusing on the cost of living and the government’s handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year’s presidential election, according to France 24’s Antonia Kerrigan in Paris.
summary: Thousands are protesting prices, education and military spending in France and across Europe. France is preparing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of demonstrations over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election.
author: France 24

title: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone fall in Poland, Tusk calls it provocation
content: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone were reported to have come down in Poland on Friday. Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as likely an “intentional provocation” timed to coincide with European military exercises in the country for a possible post‑war mission in Ukraine. Senior Lecturer Domitilla Sagramoso of King’s College London offers additional analysis.
summary: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone were downed in Poland on Friday. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident was likely an intentional provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises.
author: France 24

title: EU and Indonesia sign major trade deal after ten years of talks
content:
The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal after ten years of negotiations. The agreement removes 98.5 % of tariffs between the two parties.

For the EU, the deal opens access to a market of 280 million people and provides a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, it eases exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear and comes just before its current EU trade preferences expire on 1 January.

Airlangga Hartarto, Indonesia’s Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, joined the programme to discuss the agreement.
summary: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade agreement that removes 98.5% of tariffs between them. The deal gives Europe access to a market of 280 million people and steadier nickel supplies, while Indonesia gains easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear before its EU trade preferences end on January 1.
author: France 24

title: Fire at Banten confectionery factory kills three, leaves dozens missing
content: A fire at a confectionery factory in Indonesia’s Banten province has killed at least three people. Dozens remain unaccounted for after the blaze destroyed large parts of the facility.
summary: A fire at a confectionery factory in Indonesia's Banten province killed at least three people. Dozens remain unaccounted for after the blaze destroyed large parts of the facility.
author: DW World

title: Midwife Anisa Fadhl flees Taiz as fighting escalates, clinic looted
content: When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl fled without time to pack, abandoning her home and clinic. Both the residence and the clinic were later looted and destroyed.
summary: Fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz in southwestern Yemen two months ago. Midwife Anisa Fadhl fled without packing, leaving her home and clinic, which were later looted and destroyed.
author: UN News

title: Virginia Reports First Measles-Associated Death of 2026
content: Virginia’s health department announced that a child aged four or younger died on Friday, marking the state’s first measles‑associated death of 2026. The child tested positive for measles, and the department did not release further details, including vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy. The death comes amid a national measles outbreak that has recently led the United States to lose its measles elimination status after 26 years.
summary: Virginia's health department confirmed a child aged four or younger died after testing positive for measles, marking the state's first measles‑associated death in 2026. The department did not disclose the child's vaccination status, citing family privacy.
author: Guardian World

title: Over 20 Labour MPs enroll in leadership course funded by Gary Lubner
content:
More than 20 Labour MPs have enrolled in a year‑long leadership course designed to help them counter right‑wing populism and manage hostility. The training, which costs about £9,600 per participant, is run by former No 10 advisers and funded by multimillionaire donor Gary Lubner, who has contributed over £11 million to the party.

The programme is led by Ruth Turner, who served as Tony Blair’s director of government relations, and Peter Hyman, who has worked for the governments of Blair, Keir Starmer and Andy Burnham.
summary: More than 20 Labour MPs have signed up for a year‑long leadership course to counter rightwing populism and deal with hostility. The course, led by former No 10 advisers Ruth Turner and Peter Hyman, is funded by Gary Lubner, who has given more than £11m to Labour, and costs about £9,600.
author: Guardian World

title: Europe enters supercycle of national elections that could test EU foundations
content:
Europe is about to experience a “supercycle” of national elections, and analysts say the results could test the European Union’s stability. The article frames the upcoming polls as potentially pivotal for the bloc’s future.

To illustrate the significance of such electoral waves, the piece recalls the political landscape of late 1998. At that time, Tony Blair served as Britain’s prime minister, Lionel Jospin led France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU comprised 15 member states, with pro‑European, centre‑left parties governing all but two of them. The period was marked by brisk economic growth, ongoing eastward enlargement, and a sense of historical momentum, mirrored in the United States by President Bill Clinton’s “third way” centrism.
summary: Europe is entering a supercycle of national elections. The outcomes could become key tests of the EU’s resilience and potentially shake its foundations.
author: Guardian World

title: Outrage as Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex turned into war‑room for military AI event
content: Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads. On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.
summary: On 11 November, the central hall of the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex was transformed into a war‑room‑style setting for a military AI event hosted by an arms firm, featuring maps, aerial footage, drones, guards in flak jackets and sniffer dogs. The transformation provoked outrage, with critics calling it a serious error of judgment.
author: Guardian World

title: Former NSW MP and Christian Democratic leader Rev Fred Nile dies at 92
content:
The Rev Fred Nile, a former member of the New South Wales Legislative Council and long‑time figurehead of the right‑wing Christian Democratic Party, died at the age of 92. Nile had served in the state’s upper house for more than 40 years, first entering in 1981 and retiring after an unsuccessful bid in the 2023 election.

Known for his controversial stances, Nile frequently opposed drug use, abortion and homosexuality, yet later supported legislation to expunge homosexual convictions. His death marks the end of a lengthy career in New South Wales politics.
summary: Former NSW MP and Christian Democratic leader Rev Fred Nile dies at 92.
author: Guardian World

title: Victoria's electricity at risk as Yallourn coal plant closes by 2028, parties lack plan
content:
Victoria’s electricity supply is set to face a shortfall when the Yallourn coal‑fired power station, which has operated in the Latrobe Valley since the 1970s and provides about one‑fifth of the state’s energy, is scheduled to close in less than two years. Experts have warned that the impending loss of the plant’s output leaves the state vulnerable to power shortages and higher electricity bills.

Both major parties contesting the upcoming state election – Labor and the Coalition – acknowledge that Yallourn is at the end of its functional life, but analysts say neither party has presented a clear plan to replace the capacity the plant will provide. The lack of detailed strategies has prompted concerns that Victoria may not be able to fill the gap created by the closure.

The issue has been highlighted by climate and environment editor Adam Morton, who invites readers to subscribe to his free “Clear Air” newsletter for further coverage.
summary: The Yallourn coal‑fired power station, which supplies about one‑fifth of Victoria’s electricity, is set to close in less than two years, creating a supply gap. Experts say neither Labor nor the Coalition has an adequate plan to replace the lost capacity ahead of the state election.
author: Guardian World

title: Joshua Howard, 31, killed in suspected hit‑and‑run; body found 12 days later
content:
Police have identified the man whose body was found in Sydney bushland after 12 days as 31‑year‑old Joshua Howard. Authorities say Howard is believed to have been struck by a car and thrown over a guardrail while walking home from a party in Rouse Hill. He was last seen at a Parramatta bus interchange at about 10 p.m. on 7 November.

Howard’s twin brother said the discovery has left him feeling “like half a person.” The incident is being treated as a suspected hit‑and‑run.
summary: Joshua Howard, 31, is believed to have been struck by a car and thrown over a guardrail while walking home from a party in Rouse Hill. He was last seen at a bus interchange in Parramatta about 10 pm on 7 November, and his body was discovered 12 days later in Sydney bushland.
author: Guardian World

title: South Korea education minister resigns amid AI‑assisted exam cheating scandal
content:
South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday after an AI‑assisted cheating scandal surfaced in the run‑up to the nation’s university entrance examinations. The controversy intensified after the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam admitted using a miniature camera and a smartphone to obtain a near‑perfect result, an incident reported just four days before the pivotal “suneung” university exam.

Choi Kyo‑jin said he “failed to prepare adequately” for entrance exams, noting that this year phones were banned and officials conducted checks for hidden cameras in clothing. The scandal has heightened concerns about AI‑enabled cheating in South Korean exams.
summary: South Korea education minister resigns amid AI‑assisted exam cheating scandal.
author: Guardian World

title: Teen gamer Landon Tresp and mother aid FBI in kidnapping rescue
content: Sixteen‑year‑old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl while playing an online game. The encounter prompted Tresp and his mother to assist the FBI in locating and rescuing the girl from a kidnapping. Their involvement helped the agency secure the missing teen’s release.
summary: Sixteen‑year‑old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl while playing an online game. He and his mother then assisted the FBI in rescuing her from a kidnapping.
author: BBC World

title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
content:
Aston Villa were held to a 0‑0 draw at Villa Park by Sunderland, a result that left the visitors’ manager, Régis Le Bris, celebrating a “triumph of sorts.”  The match saw Villa’s seven shots on target largely miss, with only one—an unremarkable effort by Ian Maatsen—coming from inside the box.  The game highlighted Villa’s struggles against a disciplined Sunderland defence, a side that had been “backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay.”

Villa’s starting lineup was largely unchanged from their 4‑3‑3 encounter with Sunderland seven months earlier, with Maatsen the only player to feature in both matches.  The team was criticised for being “too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line.”  Several players were left out of the squad, including Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho, who has played only 38 minutes in the Premier League this season, and Tammy Abraham, the April match‑winner, who is expected to move in January.  Injuries, a summer of change, and the manager’s decision to rest John McGinn ahead of a Galatasaray match also influenced the selection.
summary: For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Darren Lehmann denies knowledge of 2018 sandpaper plan
content:
Former Australian Test coach Darren Lehmann has denied any knowledge of a plan to use sandpaper to alter the ball during the 2018 Test tour of South Africa. His statement directly contradicts the claims made by Cameron Bancroft, who implicated Lehmann in his detailed account of the incident. Bancroft’s statement, which exceeded 4,000 words, described the events leading to the Western Australian being discovered with sandpaper concealed in his trousers in Cape Town.

Lehmann stated that his version of events regarding the 2018 tour remains unchanged. He emphasized the need to move on from the ball tampering saga, asserting that he was unaware of any such plan.
summary: Former Australia Test coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowing about a plan to use sandpaper to alter the ball during the 2018 South Africa tour. His statement contradicts claims made by Cameron Bancroft regarding the events that led to the ball tampering incident.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England hail ‘inspirational’ Lewis Moody after thrashing New Zealand
content:
England celebrated a 37‑12 victory over New Zealand at Twickenham, the widest margin the All Blacks have ever lost to a northern‑hemisphere side. The match was highlighted by the presence of former England captain Lewis Moody, who has motor neurone disease. Moody joined the English team on the pitch for the pre‑match haka, presented the players with their shirts, and addressed the squad before the game.

England’s skipper Maro Itoje said Moody’s appearance “gave us an extra lift” and helped fuel the team’s performance. Itoje praised Moody as an inspirational player and noted that the players “jumped at the opportunity to support him.” The victory marked England’s fifth consecutive Test win, and the team credited their success in part to the support shown for Moody and his family.
summary: England hail ‘inspirational’ Lewis Moody after thrashing New Zealand.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Raya injured, Madueke secures point for Arsenal in Newcastle draw
content:
Arsenal secured a draw against Newcastle in a match marked by an early injury to Raya and a late rescue by Madueke. The article notes that Mikel Arteta, who previously disliked facing Eddie Howe’s team, found this trip to St James’ Park equally challenging. Newcastle, now managed by Matthias Jaissle, initially struggled but mounted a strong second-half comeback to earn a point.

Although the crowd appeared critical of Jaissle at half-time, he maintained composure and implemented a triple substitution with tactical adjustments. These changes proved effective, helping Newcastle fight back against Arsenal in what was described as a seesaw encounter.
summary: Arsenal's striker Raya was injured in the match against Newcastle. Madueke's goal secured a point for Arsenal in a seesaw draw at St James’ Park.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Coventry beat Palace in Frank's first game after late own goal
content: Coventry City beat Crystal Palace 3‑2, thanks to an 85th‑minute own goal by Dwight McNeil. The victory lifts the Sky Blues three points clear of the relegation zone. It also marks Thomas Frank’s first game as Crystal Palace manager, which ended in defeat in the Premier League.
summary: An own goal by Dwight McNeil in the 85th minute gave Coventry City a 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace. The win moved Coventry three points clear of the relegation zone and was Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace, which ended in defeat in the Premier League.
author: BBC Sport

title: Arsenal draw 2-2 with Newcastle, move six points clear of top
content:
Arsenal drew 2-2 with Newcastle at St James' Park, with Noni Madueke scoring in the second half.  
The result left Arsenal, the reigning champions, six points ahead of the next team at the top of the Premier League table.
summary: Noni Madueke scored a second‑half goal to secure a 2-2 draw for Arsenal at St James' Park. The result leaves the reigning champions six points ahead at the top of the Premier League table.
author: BBC Sport

title: Leeds win at Chelsea 4-1, first Stamford Bridge victory in 27 years
content: Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds United secured a 4‑1 victory at Stamford Bridge, marking the club’s first win at Chelsea in 27 years. The result lifted Leeds up to sixth place in the Premier League standings.
summary: Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds United defeated Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge, their first win there in 27 years. The result moved Leeds up to sixth place in the Premier League.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cruz and Talarico to push Texas Space Academy
content: Sen. Ted Cruz (R‑Texas) said he had a productive conversation with Sen.-elect James Talarico (D‑Texas) about the Space Academy. Cruz noted that the two will push to bring President Trump’s proposed Space Academy to Texas, adding that he spent roughly a half‑hour on the phone with Talarico.
summary: Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) said he had a productive conversation with Sen.-elect James Talarico (D-Texas), his soon-to-be Texas partner, and that they will both push to bring President Trump’s proposed Space Academy to Texas.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says FBI database breach could offer learning opportunity
content: President Trump said Saturday the potential breach of the FBI’s nationwide criminal information database is “not good,” but it may provide an opportunity to “learn things that we would have never learned otherwise.” “I always like to put things on a positive spin,” Trump said during a phone interview with Fox News’s “Saturday in America”…
summary: Trump says FBI database breach could offer learning opportunity.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Praises Jeffries's Speakership Nod Amid Stephen Miller Criticism
content: President Trump praised House Speaker‑designate Hakeem Jeffries on Saturday morning after Jeffries described Trump’s chief of staff Stephen Miller as a “stone‑cold racist.” In a Fox News interview with Kayleigh McEnany on “Saturday in America,” Trump defended Miller, calling him a “good person.”
summary: Trump Praises Jeffries's Speakership Nod Amid Stephen Miller Criticism.
author: The Hill

title: Trump seeks 10% cap on credit card rates, willing to work with Democrats
content: President Trump reupped his call for a 10 percent cap on credit card interest rates, saying he would be willing to work with Democrats on the issue. “I didn’t even know they said it but they’ve been trying to get that for years. I would do it,” Trump said during a phone call interview with…
summary: President Trump reiterated his support for a 10 percent cap on credit card interest rates and said he would work with Democrats to achieve it. In a phone interview, he noted that Democrats had been pursuing the cap for years and that he would support it.
author: The Hill

title: Trump defends former press secretary Katie Zacharia amid California bar probe
content: President Trump praised former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia in a phone interview on Saturday, telling Fox News host Kayleigh McEnany that he had seen “the way she was being treated” and urged her not to stay in the role. He defended Zacharia’s rapid departure earlier this fall, noting his support amid a California state‑bar investigation.
summary: President Trump praised former White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia in a phone interview on Saturday. He defended her quick exit from the role earlier this fall while speaking with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany amid a California state bar investigation.
author: The Hill

title: Trump’s GOP grip tested as MAGA allies, including Elon Musk, exit
content: President Trump’s control of the Republican Party is facing serious challenges following the recent midterm elections, as prominent members of his “Make America Great Again” movement are departing. Elon Musk publicly declared he is “not MAGA,” marking a sharp reversal from his position after Trump’s inauguration.
summary: President Trump's grip on the Republican Party is being seriously tested after the midterm thumping as stalwarts of his MAGA movement flee. Elon Musk said he is “not MAGA,” reversing his stance after Trump’s inauguration.
author: The Hill

title: Hubbard Leads Foxx by 330 Votes After Recount in NC-5
content: Democrat Chuck Hubbard stays ahead of incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx after a nearly finalized recount that changed only one vote. Hubbard leads by 330 votes in North Carolina’s 5th Congressional District. Decision Desk HQ, The Hill’s nonpartisan election results partner, has not projected a winner.
summary: Democrat Chuck Hubbard remains in the lead over incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx after a nearly finalized recount that changed only one vote. Hubbard leads by 330 votes in the North Carolina 5th Congressional District race, but Decision Desk HQ has not projected a winner.
author: The Hill

title: Harvard and UC San Diego researchers map large brain volumes at nanoscale detail
content: Researchers at Harvard Medical School and UC San Diego have accelerated an imaging technique, enabling the mapping of large volumes of brain tissue at nanoscale detail for the first time. This approach reveals fine structures that connectomes can miss.
summary: Researchers at Harvard Medical School and the University of California San Diego accelerated an imaging technique to map large volumes of brain tissue in nanoscale detail. The new approach reveals fine structures that traditional brain wiring maps, or connectomes, can miss.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Chenfeng Ke's team creates sugar-based hydrogel that strengthens with repeated bending
content: Most materials get weaker with use, but a polymer developed by Chenfeng Ke’s team at Washington University in St. Louis resists wear, defying the usual laws of wear and tear.
summary: Most materials get weaker with use. A team led by Chenfeng Ke, a professor of chemistry in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, has created a polymer that defies the usual laws of wear and tear.
author: Phys.org

title: Mexican special forces capture drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa
content: Mexican special forces captured drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “Chapo Isidro”, during a raid in Sinaloa, with footage showing soldiers escorting him into an army vehicle.
summary: Mexican special forces captured drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “Chapo Isidro”, during a raid in Sinaloa. Video shows soldiers escorting the FBI most-wanted cartel boss into an army vehicle.
author: Euronews

title: Iran attacks US bases in Bahrain as it readies tankers to break US blockade
content: Iran has attacked U.S. bases in Bahrain. According to the report, the “no war, no peace” U.S.–Iran confrontation is moving toward a possible breaking point as Iran steps up military actions in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, and a critical attempt to break the U.S. naval blockade in the Persian Gulf appears imminent.
summary: Iran attacks US bases in Bahrain as it readies tankers to break US blockade.
author: Euronews

title: Dashcam video shows Russian projectile hitting Lviv building, killing two
content: A dashcam video shows a Russian projectile hitting a building directly ahead of a car in Lviv, causing the driver to reverse. The strike resulted in two fatalities and injured at least ten people.
summary: A dashcam recorded a Russian projectile striking a building directly ahead of a car in Lviv, causing a massive explosion. The attack killed two people and injured at least 10 others.
author: Euronews

title: Maltese-flagged cargo ship stranded off south-west France after grounding
content: A Maltese‑flagged cargo ship ran aground off the south‑western coast of France and remains stranded. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent the vessel from capsizing and to avoid possible pollution. The ship was not carrying cargo, and all 19 crew members were safely evacuated by helicopter, Dan Quinlan reports.
summary: A Maltese-flagged cargo ship ran aground off the south‑western coast of France and remains stranded. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent capsizing, and the vessel, which was not carrying cargo, had its 19 crew members safely evacuated by helicopter.
author: France 24

title: Mexico military captures drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores after firefight
content: Mexico’s military announced Saturday that it captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a suspected drug lord known as “El Chapo Isidro” and listed among the FBI’s ten most‑wanted fugitives. The operation resulted in a firefight that killed seven suspected attackers and four soldiers, after which Flores was flown to Mexico City.
summary: Mexico's military forces captured suspected drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro", after a deadly firefight. The clash left seven suspected attackers and four soldiers dead, and Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most‑wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City.
author: France 24

title: France sees sixth consecutive Saturday of protests over cost of living
content: France is experiencing a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, as demonstrators take to the streets to protest the rising cost of living and the government’s handling of recent social unrest. The demonstrations come ahead of next year’s presidential election, according to France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan.
summary: France is experiencing its sixth consecutive Saturday of protests as demonstrators rally over the rising cost of living. The protests also target the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election.
author: France 24

title: Russian ballistic missile hits Zelensky's hometown, kills two
content: A Russian ballistic missile struck President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday, killing two people and wounding dozens. Hours later, Zelensky said Ukraine remains determined to join NATO. The incident was reported by FRANCE 24’s Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.
summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO.
author: France 24

title: Russian missile strike on Zelensky's hometown kills two, Ukraine reaffirms NATO ambition
content: A Russian ballistic missile struck President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday, killing two people and wounding dozens. Hours later, Zelensky restated Ukraine’s determination to join NATO, responding to proposals offering Kyiv security guarantees comparable to those of the alliance.
summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO after proposals to give Kyiv security guarantees similar to those of the alliance.
author: France 24

title: Experts doubt COP summit effectiveness as US sends no delegation and delays mount
content:
The recent COP summit has been described as possibly the worst on record. Critics point to limited political leadership, the absence of an official U.S. delegation, and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, all of which raise doubts about the negotiations’ effectiveness.

Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, called the process “labyrinthine” and ultimately dispiriting, underscoring the procedural challenges faced by delegates.

France 24’s Gavin Lee interviewed climate advocate and six‑time COP delegate Henna Hundal to discuss what these issues mean for the future of global climate action.
summary: Is this the worst COP summit on record? With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations.
author: France 24

title: France sees lower turnout on sixth Saturday of cost‑of‑living protests
content: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests over the cost of living saw a drop in participation. The interior ministry reported 82,500 people across the country, while organisers claimed 150,000 attended, a decline from the 200,000 they cited last week. The demonstrations remained largely peaceful.
summary: Turnout was down at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests over the cost of living, with the interior ministry reporting 82,500 participants nationwide. Organisers claimed 150,000 people took part, down from 200,000 the previous week.
author: France 24

title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud for marathon coalition talks
content:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right‑wing Likud party to coalition talks, according to his centrist Yashar party. The invitation was announced on Saturday.

The Yashar party said the “marathon series of talks” will begin on Sunday, underscoring a commitment to form “the broadest possible government” after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.
summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party to coalition talks, according to his centrist Yashar party. The talks, described as a "marathon series", will begin Sunday and aim to form the broadest possible government after the October election failed to produce an outright winner.
author: France 24

title: Vance Refrains from Endorsing Trump’s Claim Iran Near Nuclear Weapon
content:
At a White House news conference on Friday, Vice‑President JD Vance said it was not his place to second‑guess President Donald Trump, but he stopped short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that the United States should go to war with the Islamic Republic.  

During the briefing, Trump was asked about his recent report that he was unhappy with Vance’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war. The vice‑president’s remarks did not affirm the president’s assertion.
summary: Vice‑president JD Vance said it was not his place to second‑guess President Trump, but he did not endorse the former president’s claim that Iran was close to a nuclear weapon in February. During the briefing, Trump was asked about his unhappiness with Vance’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump orders contractors to consult White House before responding to congressional inquiries
content:
Donald Trump issued an executive order late Friday directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with the White House before responding to any congressional inquiries. The order, which aims to pre‑empt a surge of Democratic requests, requires companies to withhold communications the White House deems privileged and to coordinate with the administration and other U.S. agencies on “appropriate responses” to such requests.

The order warns that contractors who do not comply risk having their contracts terminated and future work with the federal government suspended. The directive is intended to limit oversight efforts by ensuring that any communication to Congress is vetted by the Trump administration.
summary: Donald Trump issued an executive order directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult the White House about any congressional inquiries they receive. The order warns that failure to comply could result in contract termination and suspension of future federal work.
author: Guardian World

title: Louisiana man Jared Schurr charged with murders of trail victim and co‑worker with crossbow
content:
Jared Schurr, 36, was arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities say. The arrest follows two separate killings: on November 11, Schurr strangled Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, on a hiking trail north of New Orleans; on November 13, he killed his co‑worker, Woodrow Scott, 37, with a crossbow.

Investigators announced on Saturday that Schurr faces second‑degree murder charges for both deaths. The incidents are described as unrelated, and the killings occurred two days apart.
summary: Jared Schurr, 36, was arrested in Mississippi after a police chase and faces second-degree murder charges for strangling 24‑year‑old Lizeht Rodriguez on a hiking trail north of New Orleans on 11 November and for killing his co‑worker Woodrow Scott, 37, with a crossbow on 13 November. Authorities say the two killings were otherwise unrelated.
author: Guardian World

title: Man charged with attempted murder after councillor stabbed in Bradford
content: A man has been charged with attempted murder after a local councillor was stabbed while working in the community in Bradford, West Yorkshire, police said. The suspect, identified as Arfan Ali, is also facing charges of assault and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place. Police reported that Arfan Ali, described as 31 in one statement and 32 in another, is accused of attacking Ibrar Ali, a 52‑year‑old councillor, at about 11 a.m. on Thursday.
summary: Man charged with attempted murder after councillor stabbed in Bradford.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian neo-Nazis raise hundreds of thousands on GiveSendGo; White Australia party gets $200k
content: GiveSendGo has been accused of facilitating the financing of extremism, but the platform says it does not ‘condone racism, discrimination, hate speech, or violence of any kind’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Australian neo-Nazis have raised hundreds of thousands of dollars on the global crowdfunding platform GiveSendGo, which has been accused of facilitating the financing of hate and extremism. Of the 68 Australian fundraisers on the site, the White Australia party has raised the fourth-highest amount of money with $200,000 for its high court battle to overturn its ban as a designated hate group.
summary: Australian neo-Nazis have raised hundreds of thousands of dollars on the crowdfunding platform GiveSendGo. Among 68 Australian fundraisers, the White Australia party raised the fourth‑highest amount, $200,000, to fund its High Court challenge to overturn its ban as a designated hate group.
author: Guardian World

title: Queensland LNP faces reckoning over broken health system after preventable deaths claim
content: A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast At the beginning of another Queensland parliamentary sitting week, anonymous sources were out in force, this time background briefing against the state’s Labor leader, Steven Miles. It is no great revelation to observers of Queensland politics that Miles, still seemingly bruised from his election loss two years ago, has struggled to find his feet as opposition leader. Many wondered why he wanted to stay on after the party’s drubbing in 2024. Some of Labor’s factional whisperers were telling anyone who would listen that the former premier’s leadership would come to an end in the weeks before Christmas.
summary: The Queensland Liberal National Party, in government for more than two years, is being forced to accept responsibility for a broken health system linked to preventable deaths. Anonymous sources have briefed parliamentarians against Labor leader Steven Miles, who remains challenged after his party’s 2024 election loss.
author: Guardian World

title: Man in his 20s found dead after police officer shot at Whitemark, Flinders Island
content:
A police officer was shot at about 9:45 pm on Saturday night while on duty at the Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, north‑east of Tasmania. The officer remains in a serious but stable condition, Tasmanian authorities said.  

Police who were sent to investigate the shooting discovered the body of a man in his 20s nearby. Authorities have linked the deceased to the shooting incident.  

The investigation involves two firearm incidents in the small Tasmanian town, with police continuing to probe the circumstances surrounding both events.
summary: Police discovered the body of a man in his 20s near Whitemark police station on Flinders Island while responding to a shooting. An on‑duty officer was shot at about 9.45 pm on Saturday night and is in serious but stable condition.
author: Guardian World

title: Star Trek: First Contact Turns 30 as Patrick Stewart's Final Film Legacy
content: Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing, there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard. "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. It's not quite "Khan", of course — what is? — but it deserves to be mentioned in the same breath. (Image credit: Paramount) In 1996, the "odd numbers bad, even numbers good" rule of "Trek" films still, more or less, rang true. 1994's "Generations", rushed out a few months after " The Next Generation " ended its seven-year run on TV, had done decent business, but the seventh movie's convoluted "passing the baton" storyline had left many fans cold. Now, however, with Kirk killed off, it was time for Picard and his crew to explore the big-screen frontier alone. William Shatner actually pitched a resurrection storyline for Kirk, but "Trek" executive producer/overlord Rick Berman ruled that it was a little too soon to bring the good captain back. Instead, he hired "Generations" scripters and "TNG"/"Deep Space Nine" writers' room regulars Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore to craft an eighth movie capable of living up to its even-numbered predecessors. While "Generations" had been written to an extremely restrictive brief, Braga and Moore were given much more freedom the second time out. Berman was keen on a time-travel storyline while Braga lobbied for the fan-favorite Borg, and early on they explored the idea of taking the Collective back to Renaissance Italy. These plans were abandoned when Stewart vetoed the idea of wearing tights. (Image credit: Paramount) They eventually zeroed in on April 5, 2063, the date Zefram Cochrane (a character who'd previously appeared in Original Series episode "Metamorphosis") made humanity's first warp flight and put Earth on the radar of a passing Vulcan ship. "We landed on the idea of what I called the 'Star Trek' nativity scene — the birth of 'Star Trek'," Braga said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Mark A Altman and Edward Gross. "The three wise Vulcans who arrive on Earth and step out of their ship for our first contact with an extraterrestrial species. And the Borg were going to prevent that from happening, which really struck a bullseye for me, because it would allow non-'Star Trek' people to understand why 'Star Trek' matters by putting the crew and the Borg back in that time frame. I thought it would appeal to a larger audience. 'Star Trek' itself was at stake, and that was super cool to me." (Image credit: Paramount) Paramount reportedly flirted with big-name directors like Ridley Scott (" Alien ", " Blade Runner ") and John McTiernan ("Predator", "Die Hard"), before settling on Jonathan Frakes. Although this would be Frakes' first movie, the man best known for playing Commander Riker had directed numerous "Trek" episodes. Berman believed that an understanding of the franchise's DNA was more important than big-screen experience. The film wastes little time on exposition for "Trek" newbies, with just a short dream sequence to explain away Picard's history with the Borg. With a single Borg Cube on course for Earth, the Federation fleet mobilizes to fight them off. They're getting their asses well and truly kicked, too, until the Enterprise warps into the battle. The Cube is ultimately destroyed but still manages to dispatch a Sphere, which uses chronometric particles to travel back to 2063 in order to assimilate Earth in the past. Picard has no choice but to follow them back to "repair whatever damage they've done". (Image credit: Paramount) They arrive in a post-World War III Montana, where Cochrane has constructed his prototype faster-than-light vessel, the Phoenix. Played by "Babe" star James Cromwell (who'd already guest-starred in a trio of "TNG" episodes), Cochrane is some way from the man future history has remembered: a hard-drinking womanizer more motivated by potential riches than the betterment of mankind. A man uncomfortable with the idea that a high school will one day bear his name. But as some of the crew work to repair the damage caused by the Sphere's bombing raid, there are bigger problems in orbit. Borg survivors have beamed on board the Enterprise and started assimilating the vessel and its crew. Initial drafts of the script saw Riker leading the ship-based resistance while Picard remained on Earth, but — at Stewart's request — Braga and Moore flipped things round to bring the captain face-to-face with his nemesis. It proved to be a really smart move, as Stewart got to ditch his new-look Starfleet uniform and run around the Enterprise as a full-on action hero in a John McClane-style vest. (Image credit: Paramount) These Borg had been given a multiplex upgrade, with massively improved prosthetics and new extendable tendrils that injected nanoprobes to assimilate a victim from within. Frakes played up the horror aspects of the Collective, portraying them as a horde of mindless cybernetic zombies, while using "Alien" and " Aliens " as inspiration. "[Ridley Scott and James Cameron] made it clear that when it comes to villains, the more that's suggested, the scarier they are," Frakes explained. "I tried to get that with the Borg." The biggest change came at the head of the organization, where — at the suggestion of Paramount executive Jonathan Dolgen — "First Contact" introduced a previously unseen Borg Queen (brilliantly played by Alice Krige) to act as spokesperson for the Collective. (Image credit: Paramount) Bringing a singular entity to a civilisation built on the notion that there's no "I" in "team" was a controversial move, but it made perfect dramatic sense. Indeed, a legion of drones would have little chance of seducing Data, even if it was just for 0.68 seconds. "We wrestled with it quite a bit before we committed to [the Borg Queen's] character," Moore told Syfy Wire, "because it was a choice that was also antithetical to the idea of the Borg. The whole concept of these villains was that they were a collection, and that there were no individuals. And that's what made them the faceless, implacable 'resistance is futile' enemy. But it also limited how to deal with them dramatically because it meant that any scenes you always had to deal with this sort of collective voice. We decided that the story would be better if we had some individual to deal with." The Queen was also granted one of the greatest entrances in sci-fi history, as her head and torso were lowered into a robot body with a bit of help from Industrial Light & Magic. (Image credit: Paramount) The Starfleet armada's assault on the Borg was similarly impressive and effectively a test run for "The Phantom Menace", as ILM's visual effects supervisor John Knoll pioneered the CG effects pipeline that would later become pivotal to the "Star Wars" prequels. It was also a brilliant excuse to introduce several new starship designs to the "Trek" canon. They're standout moments in a film that made the most of its comparatively puny budget of $45 million (reported). (For comparison, " Independence Day ", which was released the same year — and also featured Brent Spiner — cost closer to $75 million.) As Moore later recalled in an interview with the Hollywood Reporter, "Paramount had their formula. They said that 'Star Trek' movies only make this amount of money. So, therefore, you can only have this amount of budget to make it. And, at that point, we were still — just like on the TV show — counting phaser beam effects shots [to keep the price down]." (Image credit: Paramount) The studio needn't have worried. "First Contact" was a huge hit with fans and became one of the franchise's highest-grossing films at the box office. Borg mythology introduced here (including the Queen) would become a mainstay on "Star Trek: Voyager", while Jean-Luc would get to face his cybernetic white whale again in "Picard" — though the incomparable Stewart arguably never again had another "Trek" scene to rival the ones he had here. "Fortunately it happened to be a wonderful script, and my job was not to screw it up," said Frakes. "It also holds up as a movie that just happens to be a 'Star Trek' movie, which we were all hoping would be the case." title: Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovers speed of light in 1676
content:
On November 21, 1676, Danish astronomer Ole Rømer presented his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences, announcing the discovery of the finite speed of light. Prior to this revelation, scientists generally believed that light traveled instantaneously. Rømer’s breakthrough came almost by accident while he was studying Jupiter’s moon Io, intending to use its orbital period as a cosmic clock.

For years, Rømer observed Io disappearing behind Jupiter and reappearing on the other side. He noted that these eclipses occurred every 42 hours, but the timing was not consistent. Specifically, when Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses occurred 11 minutes early, while when the two planets were farthest apart, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer identified this pattern and made an accurate prediction for an Io eclipse on November 9, 1676, before formally presenting his conclusions on November 21.

The understanding that light has a constant speed proved to be a key development for gauging the scale of the universe and developing modern physics. As explained by Live Science, the speed of light acts as an ultimate speed limit, meaning objects with mass, such as cars or neutrinos, cannot reach it because doing so would require infinite energy.
summary: On Nov. 21, 1676, Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light by noting that Io’s eclipses were 11 minutes early when Earth was closest to Jupiter and 11 minutes late when farthest. He presented his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences, concluding that light travels at a finite speed.

content:
Australia defeated England by three wickets with one ball remaining in a gripping T20 opener at the MCG. The home side, described as light on star names, chased down a target of 188 to secure the victory. The match provided a brief respite for Australian cricket following a bruising week, ending with cheers from the crowd.

title: Alcaraz defeats Shelton to reach ATP Finals
content:
Carlos Alcaraz, the second seed, secured a 3‑6, 6‑3, 7‑6(1) victory over Ben Shelton, the third seed, in the ATP Finals semi‑final in Turin. The match featured a sensational 7‑1 tie‑break, and Alcaraz maintained focus after an uncertain start to reach the final.

Shelton’s campaign was highlighted by a surprising coaching change. He hired former No 1 Juan‑Carlos Ferrero as his new coach, working alongside his father Bryan. Ferrero is described as one of the most highly respected coaches on tour and is noted for knowing Alcaraz better than any other coach.

The event took place in Turin on Saturday afternoon, where the winner, Alcaraz, advanced to the ATP Finals final.
summary: Second seed Carlos Alcaraz defeated third seed Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) to reach the ATP Finals. Shelton has hired former No 1 Juan-Carlos Ferrero as his new coach alongside his father Bryan.

title: Graham and McConnell hat-tricks lead Scotland to 11-try win over Japan
content:
Scotland defeated Japan 67‑5 in a Nations Championship match, scoring 11 tries in total. The hosts’ Ollie Smith added two tries, while Scotland’s Darcy Graham and Liam McConnell each finished with hat‑tricks, driving the team to a comfortable victory over a meek Japan side.

Graham’s hat‑trick took his career tally to 41 tries, moving him six points clear of Duhan van der Merwe at the top of Scotland’s all‑time scoring charts. McConnell, the 22‑year‑old back‑rower, broke his Scotland duck with a treble of his own, marking a memorable day for the young player.
summary: Scotland defeated Japan 67-5 in the Nations Championship, scoring 11 tries. Darcy Graham and Liam McConnell each scored a hat-trick, with Graham reaching 41 career tries and McConnell ending his Scotland try drought.

title: Williams-Barnett becomes youngest Premier League scorer for Tottenham, helps win over Ipswich
content:
Luca Williams‑Barnett made his first senior start for Tottenham, scoring as an 18‑year‑old and becoming the club’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007. He then provided a mesmerising, match‑winning assist to Dominic Solanke in a win over Ipswich.

The victory gave Tottenham four league wins from their last five matches under manager Roberto De Zerbi, who served a one‑match touchline ban and watched from the stands. Tottenham have struggled to match Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing home‑grown players, but Williams‑Barnett’s breakthrough suggests a new era.
summary: The 18‑year‑old Luca Williams‑Barnett became Tottenham’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007. His goal and assist helped the club secure a 4‑of‑5 league win record against Ipswich, while manager Roberto De Zerbi served a one‑match touchline ban.

title: Noah Okafor piles on pain for Alonso as rampant Leeds demolish dismal Chelsea
content:
Leeds United secured a 2-0 victory over Chelsea, marking their first win at Stamford Bridge since December 1999. The match saw Leeds dominate Chelsea, who are currently eighth in the league but have lost more league games than Manchester United. The result leaves Chelsea without European football for the upcoming season unless they improve their performance.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke’s team was described as superbly coached and dominant throughout the encounter. Noah Okafor scored two clinical goals for Leeds, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin added a penalty in the second half, which was his sixth goal of the season. A late effort from Brenden Aaronson was also mentioned in the report. Despite a controversial handball penalty awarded to Leeds, the article notes that the officials' decisions were a minor detail compared to Leeds' overall superiority.
summary: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United.

title: Slade scores five tries as England beat New Zealand 37-12
content:
England secured a decisive 37‑12 victory over New Zealand in a match played on the historic south‑west London pitch. Slade opened the scoring and went on to score the first of five tries for the home side, while Ollie Chessum added a fourth try shortly after the restart, helping England build a 19‑0 lead by the 36th minute.

The All Blacks struggled to cope with England’s clear‑eyed, motivated opposition, and at times appeared second‑rate. The loss was considered by some Kiwi fans to be as damaging to the team’s reputation as the previous week’s defeat to Wales.

With the margin of victory, England recorded New Zealand’s heaviest defeat to any northern‑hemisphere nation in the All Blacks’ proud history.
summary: England defeated New Zealand 37-12, with Slade scoring five tries. New Zealand fell behind 19-0 after 36 minutes and suffered its heaviest loss to a northern hemisphere team.

title: Ireland beat South Africa 20-17 in Nations Championship rugby match
content:
Ireland defeated South Africa 20-17 in a Nations Championship rugby union match that kicked off at 4.40pm GMT. The live coverage noted a specific sequence of play where South Africa’s poor restart drill handed possession to Ireland in a favorable attacking position.

Ireland’s Prendergast initially attempted to find space out wide, but the opportunity was closed down by Baloucoune and Baird, the latter carrying the ball from the ruck. Although Ireland’s returns diminished, the Boks committed an offside offense, providing Ireland with a tactical advantage.
summary: Ireland beat South Africa 20-17 in the Nations Championship rugby union match that began at 4.40pm GMT. A poor restart by South Africa gave Ireland an attacking advantage, but the Boks later had an offside advantage.

title: FAU and Brazil Researchers Release MyoGen, Open-Source Brain‑Spinal‑Muscle Simulation
content:
Researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) and partners in Brazil have developed the MyoGen platform, an open-source tool that integrates brain commands, spinal cord neural circuits, and muscle responses into a single simulation. The model addresses the previous isolation of these neuromotor processes in assistive system development for paralyzed individuals.

Presented in the journal Nature Communications, the freely accessible platform is designed to support clinical research and optimize medical devices.
summary: Researchers at Friedrich‑Alexander‑Universität Erlangen‑Nürnberg and partners in Brazil developed the MyoGen platform, an open‑source simulation that integrates brain commands, spinal cord circuits and muscle responses. The model, published in Nature Communications, is freely accessible and is intended to support clinical research and the optimization of medical devices.

content: Kasia Lipska, M.D., associate professor of medicine (endocrinology) at Yale School of Medicine, and her colleagues tested a new approach to incorporating patients' priorities into diabetes care. summary: In two related papers published in JAMA Network Open and the Journal of General Internal Medicine, Kasia Lipska, M. D., associate professor of medicine (endocrinology) at Yale School of Medicine (YSM) and her colleagues tested a new approach to incorporating patients' priorities into their diabetes care.

title: Study Finds Disparities in GLP-1 Drug Access for Weight Loss
content:
Glucagon‑like peptide‑1 (GLP‑1) receptor agonists have risen sharply in popularity across the United States in recent years, moving from specialized treatments for type 2 diabetes to broader uses that include weight management, cardiovascular health and other emerging indications.  

Despite this rapid growth, a new study led by researchers at Boston University School of Public Health (BUSPH) finds that not all populations are benefiting.  The research shows that as GLP‑1 use has increased, disparities in access to these drugs have widened significantly.
summary: A new study by Boston University School of Public Health shows that disparities in access to GLP-1 receptor agonists have widened as demand for the drugs rises. Many eligible patients are unable to obtain these medications for weight management.

title: Alcohol Consumption May Weaken Cancer Immunotherapy, Study Finds
content: A new study in Science Signaling suggests that regular alcohol consumption may weaken the effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy, a treatment that has transformed care for several advanced cancers. The research highlights that simple routine habits, such as drinking alcohol, could influence whether these therapies work.
summary: Science Signaling published a study indicating that regular alcohol consumption may weaken cancer immunotherapy. The research suggests that routine habits could affect the effectiveness of these advanced cancer treatments.

content: German company faced 65,000 claims from people who said they developed cancer after using weedkiller A Missouri judge on Friday approved Bayer ’s $7.25bn settlement of lawsuits ⁠alleging that its weedkiller ​Roundup causes cancer, potentially resolving litigation that has weighed on the German company for close to a decade. Judge Timothy Boyer of a state court in St Louis ⁠found the settlement “fair, reasonable and adequate”.
summary: German company Bayer faced 65,000 claims from people who said they developed cancer after using weedkiller Roundup. A Missouri judge, Timothy Boyer, approved Bayer's $7.25bn settlement of these lawsuits, calling it fair, reasonable and adequate.

title: Organ-on-a-chip platform enables assessment of environmental chemical toxicity
content: A new practical organ‑on‑a‑chip platform offers a way to evaluate the toxicity of environmental chemicals. Currently, toxicity data are available for only a small fraction of the thousands of chemicals in everyday use, and most data come from high‑dose animal studies that are costly, time‑consuming, and limited by species differences.
summary: A practical organ-on-a-chip platform can be used to assess the toxicity of environmental chemicals. Currently, toxicity information exists for only a small fraction of the thousands of chemicals used daily, and most data come from high‑dose animal studies that are costly, time‑consuming and limited by species differences.

title: El Niño Brings Heavy Snow to Sierra Nevada and Southern Rockies, Prompting Early Openings
content:
El Niño has created a skiers’ paradise in Chile, according to the headline.  

In California, El Niño brings abundant snow to the Sierra Nevada and the southern Rockies. Tahoe‑area resorts recorded several feet of snowfall in mid‑November 2026 and some opened early, though the supercharged precipitation can also pose problems.
summary: El Niño brought several feet of snow to Tahoe-area resorts in mid‑November 2026, prompting some to open early for the season. The heavy precipitation, while beneficial for skiing, can also spell trouble.

title: Fermi LAT Map Identifies 450 Cosmic Sources, Bridging MeV Gap
content:
Gamma rays, the most high‑energy type of electromagnetic radiation in the universe, have always had a blind spot. Astronomers have struggled to measure them in the megaelectronvolt (MeV) energy range, a region that has come to be known as the “MeV gap.”

A recent paper by an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, aims to close that gap. The study identifies 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range, delivering the clearest view of low‑energy gamma rays ever recorded.
summary: A new paper by the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, identifies 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range. It provides the clearest view of low‑energy gamma rays, helping to close the long‑standing MeV gap.
author: Phys.org

title: Magnitude 6.5 Earthquake Shakes Southern Africa from Kalahari Craton
content:
In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck southern Africa, originating from an unlikely source in the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. The event highlighted the seismic potential of a region long thought to be geologically stable.

The Kalahari Craton is the ancient core of the continent, composed of crustal blocks that can be up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have traditionally regarded such areas as too cold, too thick and too rigid to split apart.
summary: Magnitude 6.5 Earthquake Shakes Southern Africa from Kalahari Craton.
author: Phys.org

title: Ancient Himera Babies Started Solid Food at 3 Months, Nursed for Nearly 4 Years
content: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Chemical signatures suggest that babies in the colony began solid food at 3 months but were breastfed for nearly 4 years.
summary: Chemical signatures from ancient Himera babies show they began solid food at three months and continued nursing for nearly four years. The colony, inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks, practiced early weaning across diverse cultural backgrounds.
